editorSummary:
Kevin — 98 threads reached me. Twenty-five were the same finding filed two or three times, which is the useful part: where reviewers collided independently is where the real bugs are.

Four things deserve fixing before anything else.

1. Your service worker has never installed. One line is duplicated in sw.js, the browser rejects the whole cache list, so there is no offline mode and every sprite re-downloads on every launch (F-096).
2. When the tablet runs out of room a catch half-saves: the dex ticks the Pokémon off, but the Pokémon comes back Lv5 — or vanishes with the ball that caught it (F-091). That is the saves-are-sacred rule.
3. ROUND 2 shows ROUND 1's ticks. Gabe's champion screen says 58/58 DONE for a ladder he has not started (F-066, two reviewers).
4. Versus has no handicap. Art's Lv9 Pikachu meets Gabe's Lv62 Charizard and Art's team faints — the one place Junior Mode's promise breaks, in the mode the boys play together (F-016).

The loudest pattern, across half the forum: Art is fine wherever meaning is a picture and stranded wherever it is a word. Trainer card, PASS TO ART, quest rewards, the out-of-storage warning, CANCEL, CLOSE. Junior Mode redrew the dex, the battle buttons and the box beautifully, then stopped.

Also: mashing blanks the Junior dex — three reviewers, four saves.

The praise is specific enough to become tests: the boot faces, colour-versus-shadow in Art's box, the battle move grid, the import-and-undo path. And checked directly: the game still never speaks.

inflight.title: Cap the species cache so it can't fill the tablet
inflight.kevin: Browsing the whole Pokedex can no longer eat the room the boys' collections live in.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - the cache and the save share one 5MB box
acceptance: smoke: after seeding 400 synthetic pkmn: entries, pokedexos_apicache_v2 holds at most the cap (oldest evicted first) and its serialised length stays under 1.5MB
smoke: a cache eviction never removes or damages pokedexos_save_v2
inflight.notes: CACHE_KEY is pokedexos_apicache_v2 (api.js:10); the single writer is saveCache (api.js:14-23). There is no cap, no LRU, no TTL. The only eviction is reactive inside the quota catch (api.js:17-21): drop move: keys, retry once, then set cache={} in memory WITHOUT removeItem, so a stale on-disk blob outlives an empty in-memory view. Count entries honestly: getPokemon deliberately stores each species twice, under a name key and an id key (api.js:142-143). Most of the ~8-9KB per species is slimPokemon keeping the entire moves array (api.js:61) - trimming that is a cheaper alternative but battle move selection reads it, so price that before choosing. The file header comment ('~2-3KB each, 151 Pokemon = 450KB') is stale in two ways and should be corrected while you are in there: MAX_POKEMON is 649.

nextUp.title: Versus must not flatten Art
nextUp.kevin: Brother-versus-brother is a real match now instead of Gabe's Charizard knocking over everything Art owns.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes
Never take something away from a child
acceptance: smoke: a versus match seeded with a Lv62 team against a Lv9 team runs with both sides' effective levels within 5 of each other
smoke: no string matching /junior|easy|helper|handicap|fair/i appears anywhere in the versus DOM
nextUp.notes: This is deliberate today, and the comment says so: juniorActive() (battle.js:101-103) returns false whenever battleState.versusActive, and the header at battle.js:1804 reads 'No catching, no junior shield, no XP - pure bragging rights.' CLAUDE.md rule 2 outranks that comment; versus is the one mode the brothers play together and it is the one place the promise breaks. Prefer a LEVEL CAP (cap both sides at the lower team's top level where levels are read raw at battle.js:1808, 1850-1851, 1974) over re-enabling the one-sided shield: a cap is symmetric and invisible, whereas a shield Gabe can feel is an accommodation that advertises itself. Note juniorActive() also gates enemy AI smartness (battle.js:936), the result beat (1022) and wild level spread (306), so do not widen it - add the cap at fighter construction. versusActive is cleared only in versusMatchOver/quit (1876,1902,1992); make sure teardown resets whatever you add or the next wild battle inherits versus rules.

nextUp.title: The dex type tile gets its picture and readable ink
nextUp.kevin: The word POISON on Art's screen becomes the same purple droplet he already knows from battles.
rule_risk: Junior Mode information carried only as words
acceptance: smoke: every rendered .tag type chip on the dex contains its typeEmoji glyph
smoke: every rendered .tag type chip measures at least 4.5:1 between its own computed color and its own computed background - measured on the ELEMENT, not on inkFor() in the abstract
nextUp.notes: HIGHEST VALUE PER LINE IN THE WHOLE BACKLOG. dex.js:218 writes the bare word with a background and no colour, so .tag (gba.css:139, main.css:42 - neither declares color) inherits body{color:white} from main.css:8. White on electric #eed535 is about 1.5:1, which is F-037's measurement, and it is still true at HEAD. Both halves of the fix already exist and are already used together one file away: typeEmoji (config.js:183-192) and inkFor (config.js:217-221) are imported by battle.js:568-569 for the move tiles. dex.js imports neither. READ THIS PART TWICE: the existing smoke check 'every type chip clears WCAG AA' (smoke.mjs:1169) PASSES TODAY while the real screen fails, because it measures inkFor(colour) as a function rather than the element the child looks at. That check is giving false assurance - strengthening it is part of this item, not a nice-to-have. Note the irony in the code: dex.js:219-220's own comment says 'beside the pictures of its types'. The intent was there; the glyph never landed.

nextUp.title: A cry when a wild one appears, and when caught
nextUp.kevin: Art hears what he just met and what he just caught, instead of reading its name.
rule_risk: Junior Mode information contract: at the encounter, who just showed up exists only as words
acceptance: smoke: a wild encounter and a successful catch each fire the cry bus exactly once (spy on playCryFor)
smoke: with pokedexos_muted=1 the same two moments fire it zero times
nextUp.notes: battle.js imports only { sfx, triggerVibration, playBeep, haptic } from audio (battle.js:17) - no cry function is imported or called anywhere in the file. The cries exist and are good; they simply only ever play on the dex and in the sticker book. Use playCryFor(id) (audio.js:355): it reads the api cache directly and needs no setCry. Three things not to get wrong: respect CRY_MIN_GAP_MS (audio.js:263) so a fast catch does not stack two cries; copy the AudioContext-unlock guard from dex.js:49-52; and do NOT touch the shared setCry module global - pc.js has to hand it back after the sticker close-up (pc.js:449-454) or the home CRY button plays the wrong voice. The editor called this the highest-value cheap fix in the forum for Art and the only cluster a screenshot cannot protect - which is why B-012 exists.

backlog.title: Silence should look like silence
backlog.kevin: The button that turns the sound off stops looking like a NO sign, and it keeps its shape.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - one unlabelled tap removes Art's whole non-verbal channel
acceptance: smoke: toggling #music-btn twice leaves its .btn-glyph child element intact (assert the span still exists after each toggle)
smoke: the muted glyph string differs from #cry-btn's glyph string
backlog.notes: A real bug nobody filed sits underneath the design complaint: syncMusicBtn (settings.js:19-22) assigns btn.innerText, which DESTROYS the <span class='btn-glyph'> the markup provides (index.html:40) and replaces it with a bare text node. After the first toggle the glyph permanently loses its sizing and alignment and never gets it back. Use querySelector('.btn-glyph').textContent. Then the design half: with sound off the child sees a red prohibition circle, which to a four-year-old reads 'you are not allowed', and with sound on it is the SAME speaker glyph as the CRY button in his own toolbar. Make the off state a picture of silence (a full-size speaker with one slash, or a note fading) and give CRY a different glyph. Leave the storage alone: pokedexos_muted is deliberately device-wide, not per-player (audio.js:62, 85-90), and that is a defensible choice - the editor upheld only the legibility risk, not the sharing.

backlog.title: An uncaught shadow should still answer a poke
backlog.kevin: When Art prods a Pokemon he hasn't caught yet, something happens.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes - a dead-feeling tap teaches a four-year-old the pictures are not for touching
acceptance: scenes: tapping an uncaught .pc-item in junior mode changes at least one measured box or paint property that the baseline records, and the change is still visible 300ms after the tap
backlog.notes: THE JUNIOR HALF OF F-013 IS FALSE and the correction changes the fix entirely. Junior taps DO open a card: handlePCSelect routes straight to openSticker (pc.js:331). What the reviewer hit was an UNCAUGHT sticker, which deliberately answers with a 320ms .tease shake and no modal (pc.js:413-418) - and in the junior book every one of the 649 slots is rendered (pc.js:294), so on a fresh save every tile on screen is a grey shadow that wiggles briefly and does nothing else. The two 'byte-identical' screenshots the editor verified with md5 are consistent with the shake having simply finished before the harness fired. So the real defect is that the answer is too small and too brief to survive a four-year-old's attention, not that there is no answer. Give it something that lands and stays for a beat - a silhouette lift, a soft thud - so 'not yet' reads as an answer rather than a broken button. This is the thread F-002 is really about: a pre-reader's whole vocabulary for 'tell me about this' is poking the picture.

backlog.title: Ask before you hand over the other brother's game
backlog.kevin: One stray tap can't drop Art into Gabe's champion save any more.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - one accidental tap gives edit rights over the other brother's collection
acceptance: smoke: tapping #player-btn opens a confirm showing both players' lead sprites, and state.currentPlayer does not change until it is accepted
smoke: cancelling the confirm leaves any in-progress gym run intact
backlog.notes: togglePlayer (main.js:111-115) switches players on one tap of a chip about a centimetre wide sitting right beside the Pokeball everybody taps first, with no confirm and no undo - and it lands you in the other boy's PC box with full edit rights over his collection. The only guard is 'not mid-catch, not mid-battle'. There is a second, quieter cost the forum missed: setPlayer also calls clearGymRun (main.js:107), so a stray tap silently discards a half-finished gym run and its endurance HP. #whoplaying-modal already draws exactly the two-face card this needs (main.js:127-133) - the screen F-019 praises - so reuse it rather than inventing a dialog.

backlog.title: Stop a stale dex fetch from repainting the screen
backlog.kevin: Art can tap the arrows as fast as he likes and his Pokemon always comes back.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - mashing is how Art plays and it currently strands him with no way back
acceptance: smoke: after 20 synthetic #nav-next clicks 30ms apart and a settle, #types holds at least one .tag, #poke-sprite computed opacity is 1, and #poke-name is neither empty nor 'LOADING'
smoke: after that mash, state.curId equals the id printed in #id-text (a stale response can no longer win and re-seed the arrows)
smoke: a loadPoke() whose fetch rejects after a newer nav has started leaves #types and #stats-area untouched
backlog.notes: MECHANISM, verified in source and NOT what the forum diagnosed. There is no reveal animation that restarts and never repaints: pxReveal (fx.js:82-88) and wipeSweep both self-clear on timers longer than their own durations. The real faults are all in loadPoke (dex.js:118-186): (1) there is no in-flight token, and state.curId/state.curData are assigned AFTER the await (dex.js:132-133), so with N taps in flight the screen settles on whichever request resolves last and that stale response also re-seeds the arrows; cache hits resolve instantly while misses take network time, so out-of-order resolution is the NORMAL case when mashing. (2) The catch block (dex.js:140-155) clears #types and #stats-area with no guard at all, so a request abandoned four taps ago can wipe the chips off a Pokemon that already rendered. (3) #poke-sprite.style.opacity=0 is set at dex.js:125 BEFORE the await and only restored inside the guarded branch at 179-185, which also leaves setScanning(true) stuck on when it bails. Take one module-level token at the top of loadPoke and re-check it after EVERY await, including inside the catch. Effort 3 because it is one function but four separate resolution points and the epoch discipline has to be right.

backlog.title: Tell the four balls apart
backlog.kevin: Gabe can see which ball is better before he spends it.
rule_risk: Junior Mode must never advertise its accommodations
acceptance: smoke: the four rows of #ballpick-list carry four DIFFERENT captions
smoke: in junior mode those rows carry no caption, no odds and no count (Art's drawer stays silent)
backlog.notes: Three of the four rows in the battle ball modal (battle.js:1548-1571) carry the identical line BETTER WHEN WEAKENED, so the one thing the child is choosing between is the one thing the words refuse to tell him. The app already solves it two taps away: the dex drawer ranks them 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 100% (index.html:99-104). Carry that across. WHERE I DISAGREE WITH F-035: it proposes giving Art one/two/three pips so the ladder is a shape. Do not. Art's balls always succeed, so a ladder would be a lie, and F-119 praises this drawer specifically for keeping the secret - junior already hides .ball-count (gba.css:637). Art gets nothing new here and that is the correct outcome.

backlog.title: A grown-up can always get back into Parent Tools
backlog.kevin: If one of the boys sets the PIN, you are not locked out of your own save.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - the only in-app route back to a lost save can be claimed by a child
acceptance: smoke: with a PIN stored, the pad offers a recovery route that clears pokedexos_devpin while leaving pokedexos_save_v2 byte-identical
smoke: the recovery route cannot be completed by tapping alone - a wrong attempt leaves the gate shut and the existing 'wrong PIN keeps the pad up' check still passes
backlog.notes: requirePin (devtools.js:223-233) is trust-on-first-use: if no PIN is stored it just sets one, with no proof of who is asking. There is no removeItem of PIN_KEY anywhere in the repo, the PIN is per-device localStorage and is not in the save, and it gates PASTE CODE, LOAD FILE, UNDO IMPORT and Parent Tools - i.e. the entire restore path. The only documented way back is a devtools console command on a device with no F12. Whatever you build must not become a bypass a 7-year-old can walk: prefer something that needs an artefact the child does not have (the exported save code or file) or a long hold plus a word printed in the README. Fail closed on every branch, the way requirePin already does.

backlog.title: PASS TO shows the boy, not a controller
backlog.kevin: Art can see whose turn it is because his own Pokemon is on the card.
rule_risk: Junior Mode: Art cannot tell whose turn it is
acceptance: smoke: #pass-modal contains an img whose src is the receiving player's lead sprite, and that src differs between P1's turn and P2's turn
smoke: the #vs-btn label contains both players' lead sprites, and still renders when player 2 has never been named
backlog.notes: waitForPass (battle.js:1821-1825) sets only the h2 text; the 46px controller emoji is hard-coded in index.html:326 and is identical on both boys' cards, so nothing on screen changes between turns. The sprite is already loaded and preloaded and in scope: sideActive(n).spriteFront, from versus.sides built at battle.js:1846-1858 - a two-line change at 1822. The app already solves this correctly one screen earlier: #whoplaying-modal draws each boy's lead (main.js:127-133), which is the screen F-019 praises. F-086's 'P 2' comes from state.js:179-182's `P${n}` fallback, rendered into gym.js:155 - leave the fallback, add the sprites, and the button works on day one before anyone opens Settings. The visible gap in 'P 2' is the pixel font, not a stray space in the data.

backlog.title: One catch, one save write
backlog.kevin: If the tablet ever runs out of room mid-catch, the Pokemon and the ball can't disagree any more.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred
Never take something away from a child
acceptance: smoke: with localStorage.setItem stubbed to throw from the second call onward, a dex catch leaves the save either fully containing the new id (in caught AND in mons) or fully unchanged - never caught-without-mons, and never a spent Master Ball with no catch
smoke: a single dex catch calls persist() exactly once (counted with a spy)
backlog.notes: persist() (state.js:240-264) is the only writer and it serialises the WHOLE save each time, so no single write is itself partial - the tearing is a prefix effect across five independent persists in one catch: spendMasterBall (catch.js:49), recordCatch (catch.js:126), ensureMon (catch.js:127), the game-progress listener (catch.js:135 -> progression.js:192/302/344/350) and setNick (catch.js:144). Batch them: defer and flush once. Two things the forum got slightly wrong and the implementer must not repeat: the 'comes back as Lv5' case is caught-without-a-mons-entry falling through to DEFAULT_LEVEL (state.js:310,328), and the genuinely destructive case is the ball being spent before the catch lands. persist() returns false on failure and NO caller checks it - the flush must check and roll the in-memory save back. Do NOT change the save shape.

backlog.title: Art's trainer card, in pictures
backlog.kevin: The gold star page finally tells Art how he is doing without a single word.
rule_risk: Junior Mode accessibility: the game's only progress summary is words-only
acceptance: scenes: in junior mode #card-modal renders no .card-badge em caption and no .badge-prog fraction, and the dex count is drawn as a filled meter
scenes: the junior card's scroll height at 375x667 is under twice its box height
backlog.notes: PARTLY TRUE as filed and the difference matters: the badge GLYPHS are already pictures (shipped v19.5.3), so this is not 'Junior Mode never touched this screen' - it is that the captions, the fraction and the POKEDEX 0/649 (0%) line were left behind. Your starting point is already written: gba.css:621-625 is an ORPHANED comment describing exactly these junior overrides ('push the card to 1243px of scrolling inside a 566px box') and the body.junior .card-badge rules it documents DO NOT EXIST. Someone wrote the plan and never wrote the CSS. The exit half of this screen belongs to B-007; the clipping half belongs to B-009. Do not remove anything from Gabe's card.

backlog.title: Quest rewards Art can aim at
backlog.kevin: Art can see which quest to go and do, instead of being surprised by stars.
rule_risk: Junior Mode: the reward panel is words-only
acceptance: scenes: in junior mode the celebration panel shows a sprite or type-glyph row and contains no sentence longer than six words
smoke: the same completed quest awards identical XP in junior and normal mode
backlog.notes: One shared #badge-modal is filled by nextCelebration (progression.js:249-291) for badges, quests AND the shiny ceremony, and its only branch is item.shiny (line 277). The quest text is built at progression.js:335 as '<label> - done!\n+30 XP to your lead Pokemon!'. Junior quest SELECTION already branches (easyCount, progression.js:171) - only the telling doesn't. Say it as the type tile he needs, then the same tile with a tick; he already reads type colour fine elsewhere. Nothing is being taken away: he gets the XP either way today, he just never gets to aim, and aiming is the fun part. Fixing the shared panel also improves the badge and shiny ceremonies for free, which is why this is worth more than its thread count.

backlog.title: A picture for the moment the tablet is full
backlog.kevin: The emergency screen shows a grown-up what happened and offers to save the game right there.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred
Junior Mode: the warning cannot reach a pre-reader
acceptance: smoke: the save-failure screen renders an image or inline SVG (not only an emoji) and a button that reaches the export path in one tap
smoke: that export button is reachable without a PIN
backlog.notes: showSaveFailureBanner (state.js:268-284) is built in JS with inline cssText: a 56px warning emoji, 'SHOW A GROWN-UP', then 26 words of prose in sans-serif - a typeface this game uses nowhere else - full-screen, no dismiss, and NO WAY TO GET THE SAVE OFF THE DEVICE. It is the single most important screen in the app, it appears at the exact moment the collection is at stake, and it is the one screen written entirely in words. Art closes the app, which is exactly how the message never reaches Kevin. The export button must NOT sit behind requirePin - that gate is what B-005 is about, and a locked-out parent plus a full disk is the worst case in this whole review. There is a second variant of this screen for an unreadable save (state.js:208-211); give it the same treatment.

backlog.title: A dropped connection should not shout ERROR at Art
backlog.kevin: Losing wifi shows a sleeping Pokeball instead of the word ERROR in the biggest letters on screen.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes: the loudest thing on Art's screen is a failure that was not his fault
acceptance: scenes: with the API route aborted, the junior dex contains no string matching /ERROR|TIMEOUT|API|Server/ and #poke-sprite's src is the inline SVG fallback
smoke: two consecutive sprite failures on #poke-sprite both end at the inline SVG (the per-element fallback no longer self-disables)
backlog.notes: dex.js:140-155 writes 'ERROR / TIMEOUT' into #poke-name at whatever font size the last successful render left behind - up to 32px, the largest text the app owns - plus 'API Server issue or Pokemon not found.' into #desc, with no junior branch anywhere in loadPoke. There is a second, sharper bug underneath: dex.js:153 points the sprite at ITEM_SPRITE('poke-ball'), which is the SAME remote host that just failed, and the delegated image net in main.js:368-374 self-disables per element via dataset.fellBack. Because #poke-sprite is one long-lived img reused for the whole session, the SECOND failure leaves the browser's own broken-image glyph on screen - which is precisely the 'torn page' the reviewer photographed. FALLBACK_SPRITE (main.js:378-384) is an inline data-URI Pokeball that cannot fail; it is a module-local const today. Export it from config.js and use it here. F-099 praises this exact fallback working elsewhere - this is the one path that misses it.

backlog.title: Ticks that go somewhere permanent
backlog.kevin: Yesterday's finished quests are counted forever instead of vanishing at midnight.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - yesterday's four completed quests are deleted overnight
acceptance: smoke: completing a quest increments player.stats.questsDone; the value survives a reload and a day rollover; a save written before this change still loads with the field defaulted
backlog.notes: SCHEMA TOUCH, BUT THE SAFE KIND - follow the existing precedent exactly. stats is {catches, battlesWon, battlesLost, versusWins} (state.js:73), merged shallowly at state.js:146, and `explores` is already an undeclared latecomer written by explore.js:299 and read defensively as (p.stats.explores || 0) at progression.js:388. Do the same: additive, always defaulted on read, no version bump, no migration. p.quests is wiped whenever the day changes (progression.js:190) and allDone is per-day, so there is no aggregate anywhere today. This is not a streak and must not become one - it only ever counts up.

backlog.title: A bad second of wifi must not break a sprite
backlog.kevin: A Pokemon they caught can't lose its picture permanently.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - a caught Pokemon can permanently lose its picture
acceptance: smoke: a sprite request that fails is not written into pokedexos-assets, asserted against the caching predicate directly
smoke: an entry already stored from a failed response is re-fetched rather than served
backlog.notes: sw.js:98 accepts `resp.ok || resp.type === 'opaque'`, and an opaque response is status 0 whether it was a picture or a 404 or a rate-limit - the browser will not say which. The shell branch is strict by comparison (sw.js:79). Then nothing ever repairs it: ASSET_CACHE is the version-independent 'pokedexos-assets' (sw.js:17) and activate only deletes keys ending in '-shell' (sw.js:50), so a release bump will not clear it and nothing prunes it. One flaky minute on hotel wifi and whichever Pokemon the boys were looking at is a blank ball until someone clears site data - which is also where the saves live. Options: request sprites with an explicit cors mode so ok means something, or sanity-check the stored response's size/type. This only bites now that the worker actually installs (v19.8.1), which is why it was invisible before.

backlog.title: Yesterday's collection, kept
backlog.kevin: The game quietly keeps a spare copy every day, and tells you when you last saved one yourself.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred
acceptance: smoke: on the first boot of a new local day a dated backup key appears holding the previous save verbatim, and at most N are retained
smoke: Settings shows a LAST BACKED UP line that reads NEVER on a fresh device and a date after an export
backlog.notes: The game already knows how to hold a second save shape - it does it on every import - but only when a grown-up is standing at the Settings screen. Every other day of the year there is exactly one copy of both boys' collections, in one browser key, on one tablet. Today's only routine second copy is pokedexos_save_v2_prev (state.js:8), written ONLY by importCode (state.js:475): nothing snapshots before removeMon (devtools.js:110) or before a normal session, and restorePreviousSave writes the displaced save back into the same slot (state.js:305), so a second UNDO walks you forward again rather than two deep. There IS a dated key already - pokedexos_save_corrupt_<timestamp> (state.js:9,198) - but it is written only on an unreadable save, is never read back anywhere, and its own setItem is inside a try that gives up silently when storage is full. 21KB per copy. NO SAVE-SHAPE CHANGE: these are sibling keys. Sequence after B-004 - the backups live in the same 5MB box the cache is currently eating.

backlog.title: Grown-up Pokemon in grown-up places
backlog.kevin: Once Gabe is strong, the wild starts showing him evolved Pokemon instead of babies with big numbers.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - the low-level species must stay catchable
acceptance: smoke: over 200 rolls in a habitat whose level band is 40 or higher, no rolled species is one that evolves below that level
backlog.notes: rollEncounter (explore.js:276-284) picks a rarity tier and then a raw id from static c/u/r/L arrays; the level is computed completely separately (battle.js:304-306) and never feeds back into the species choice. So a champion meets a Lv57 Koffing - a thing that cannot exist in the wild anywhere else in Pokemon - and his dex will never once show him an evolved form appearing in the grass. Effort 3 and it is not splittable: EXPLORE must not depend on the network, so this needs a local evolution-stage table. habitatfill.js is the precedent - it is generated into the repo by a tool - so follow that pattern rather than fetching chains at runtime. Do NOT remove the base forms from the pools; swap the weighting as the band climbs, so nothing a child could previously catch becomes uncatchable.

backlog.title: Let Gabe give Art a Pokemon
backlog.kevin: The big brother can hand the little one something, with a ribbon on it.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred - this writes into a second player's save
acceptance: smoke: gifting moves a copy into the other player's save without removing the giver's last copy, and both saves stay schema-version 2 and reload cleanly
smoke: the receiving box marks the gift with the giver's lead sprite, not the word 'from'
backlog.notes: Two boxes, one device, one house, and no door between them. Effort 3 because it is the only item that writes into the OTHER player's save - the single riskiest kind of change in this codebase - and it needs a refusal path (never hand over a last copy) plus a ribbon marker that survives export/import. Follow the favourites precedent: additive, defaulted, dropped on load if it refers to something unowned (there are already smoke checks shaped exactly like that). The reason to want it is not the Pokemon: right now the only thing a 620-strong collection lets the older brother do is be further ahead, and this gives him something to do with it that makes the little one happier.

backlog.title: A gauntlet: five trainers, one health bar
backlog.kevin: Once a gym is beaten, there is a harder way to do it again that uses what is already there.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - losing a gauntlet must cost nothing
acceptance: smoke: a gauntlet run carries HP across all five trainers with no heal between them, and losing at trainer four removes nothing from the save
backlog.notes: The circuit already owns every part a tournament needs and never holds one: HP carries between trainers inside a stop, the stops are five-trainer ladders that already escalate, and badges already hang on a wall. Clear it and a ribbon lights next to that stop's badge. It is real difficulty without inventing a trainer or raising a level, and it makes a Lv8-13 roster mean something again to a Lv62 team. Rules-safe by construction: he opts in, and if he falls over at trainer four nothing is taken - he keeps the badge, keeps the Pokemon, and the ribbon is simply not lit yet. Effort 3 because it threads new state through the gym run and the battle teardown, both of which are the fragile parts of this codebase.

backlog.title: A wind-down that never takes anything away
backlog.kevin: At the end of the evening the game gets sleepy instead of shutting a door.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child - a wind-down must refuse nothing
acceptance: smoke: with a wind-down length set, nothing becomes disabled or unavailable, no timer value is written into the save, and the trainer card still records no minutes of clock
backlog.notes: Thirty-three screens of a simulated Saturday and not one of them is a resting place: the victory modal's only button is CONTINUE, the dex's two biggest buttons are EXPLORE and GYMS, and the end of a session is a wall of green REMATCH bars. Every exit is a door further in. Build this as the OPPOSITE of a lockout: after a length Kevin sets, green fades to dusk, EXPLORE and GYMS go quiet, and the PC box opens by itself on today's catches with their cries - a goodnight card made of the sprites he earned rather than a sentence. The acceptance line encodes the rule that matters: the app currently keeps no clock on the children anywhere, and the clock belongs in Kevin's hands, not in the save.

backlog.title: No half-row of Pokemon against the BACK bar
backlog.kevin: Reaching for the next row of his box no longer lands Art on the button that leaves it.
acceptance: scenes: in the pc and sticker-book scenes at 375x667, no .pc-item is left clipped to under 40% of its height at the bottom fold
backlog.notes: THE FORUM'S MECHANISM IS WRONG: #close-pc-btn declares no position at all (main.css:254, gba.css:427) and is an ordinary flex sibling BELOW .pc-grid inside a flex-column #pc-modal (main.css:240-242), and the grid already carries padding-bottom:20px. A four-year-old reaching for a partly-visible thing plants his fingertip at the top of what he can see, and the centre of that contact patch lands on BACK. Fix it by making rows land whole - scroll-padding-bottom or scroll-snap on .pc-grid - not by restacking anything.

backlog.title: Say which round you are standing in
backlog.kevin: Gabe can tell at a glance whether he is looking at the circuit he has beaten or the one he hasn't started.

Round 2 is NOT displaying Round 1's data. beatenCount, gymUnlocked, trainerUnlocked, totalBeaten and recordGymWin are all round-parameterised (gym.js:57-72, 250), trainerKey appends ':r2' (gymdata.js:178), renderGymList re-derives the round on every read (gym.js:104), and smoke already asserts 'round 2 raises every trainer by 15 and keeps round 1 untouched'. Two experienced reviewers concluded from it that the entire endgame was finished. That is the bug: gold means 'the hard good thing' AND 'selected' at the same time, and the lure wins. Give the selected tab a mark that is not a fill. T-006 and eight sibling machine threads are the missing space in the same tab's label ('CROWN-emoji' immediately followed by 'ROUND 2', gym.js:115) - fix it here while the file is open. backlog.title: SAVE FILE says what it did
backlog.kevin: The backup button tells you the filename instead of looking like nothing happened.

Two extras worth doing while you are here: revokeObjectURL fires on the very next line after click(), which can race the download in some engines; and navigator.share({files}) is supported on the boys' iPad per CLAUDE.md and appears nowhere in the repo - it is the better primitive for getting a save off a tablet. backlog.title: Play the game once with the sound on

For a pre-reader sound carries roughly half the meaning in this game and it currently has zero coverage. This item is the guard that makes B-011 stick; ship them together or ship this first. The report.json already merges across scenario runs, so adding a cries[] field per step is additive.

backlog.title: Two moves of one type must not look identical
backlog.kevin: Art's four attack buttons are four different buttons.

backlog.kevin: In the car with no signal the game still looks like itself.
acceptance: smoke: the offline shell list contains the local font file, and index.html issues no request to fonts.googleapis.com
backlog.notes: Press Start 2P is the whole voice of this app and it is the one asset that is not in the app: a remote stylesheet at index.html:11-13, absent from SHELL_FILES (sw.js:19-28), reachable only through the runtime asset branch and therefore cached only AFTER a first successful online load. So the first no-signal launch renders the entire game in Courier - legible, but a different app, and the one the boys would meet in the car. It also breaks every 8px pixel-metric the layout assumes. The woff2 is about 10KB. ASK KEVIN FIRST: committing a binary asset is the closest thing in this backlog to a build step. It is a file, not a pipeline, but CLAUDE.md says ask. Bonus: it also fixes any guest wifi that blocks Google Fonts, and it removes the reason the review corpus cannot see accented capitals (see B-051).

backlog.title: Pin down the explore map, the boot faces, the badges
backlog.kevin: The best-aimed screen in the game and the screen that lets Art pick himself both stay as they are.
acceptance: scenes: no habitat card is narrower than the content column, no vertical gap between them is under 16px, and the selected card keeps a visible ring rather than only a colour shift
scenes: #whoplaying-modal renders two lead-Pokemon images, not two text buttons
scenes: at 375 with the real pixel font loaded, every toolbar button label stays on one line at its authored size
scenes: each of the twelve gym badges has a distinct hue AND a distinct silhouette, and the earned tick sits in the same corner of every tile
backlog.notes: F-104 is the geometry every other junior screen should be measured against - 340x115 cards with 18px of dead space, about 30mm of target with 3mm of separation, and the therapist could not make Art mis-tap it if she tried. F-019 is the reason Art lands in his own game instead of arriving in his brother's and having to be rescued: it runs before the dex loads and the picture is the answer while the word is the caption. F-034's rule to keep is specific and easy to break: one uppercase word of seven characters or fewer - a future button called COLLECTION or FAVOURITES breaks the grid. That last check MUST load the real font; the harness stubs it today, so as written it would prove nothing (see B-051).

backlog.title: The gym victory tells the truth, in order
backlog.kevin: Winning a rematch stops promising a list and showing blank paper.
acceptance: smoke: after a trainer win where every spoil was already owned, #victory-lines contains no dangling 'whole team:' caption
smoke: the spoils grid's DOM position is after its own caption
smoke: a gym win names the XP number in #victory-lines the way a wild catch already does
backlog.notes: F-063 saves you the hunt and it is exactly right: setVictoryHero (battle.js:462-465) writes the grid into #victory-hero, which sits at index.html:349 - ABOVE #victory-xp (350) and #victory-lines (352), where the caption is written at battle.js:1369. So the list is not missing, it was printed about a hundred pixels higher. One correction to F-026: the grid is never empty - battle.js:1350 maps the trainer's whole team unconditionally. The lie is the word 'caught' when the child already owned all of them; the wild path handles the identical case warmly at battle.js:1522-1525 ('already in your Box') and should be the model. Two traps: #spoils-hint must keep its id because pickSpoilsFavorite rewrites it by id (battle.js:1428), and body.junior HIDES #victory-lines, which is precisely why the roster was moved into the hero half - do not move it back without checking Art's view. Everything here sits behind stale(e0) epoch guards (1348, 1374, 1389); keep them.

backlog.title: The PC generation tabs stop falling off both edges
backlog.kevin: Gabe can see and read all six tabs, including the ALL tab that holds everything.
acceptance: scenes: in the pc scene at 375x667 and 390x844 every .gen-tab's rect is fully inside the viewport and none is clipped on either edge
backlog.notes: I checked this one against the picture rather than the arithmetic and the picture wins. #gen-tabs is display:flex with justify-content:center and .gen-tab is flex:1;max-width:76px (gba.css:676-682) with no min-width:0 - so the six tabs cannot shrink below their min-content width ('G1' over '151/151' in the pixel font), they overflow the container, and centring clips them at BOTH ends. In E-0110 at 390 wide the G1 tab is sliced on the left and the ALL tab is reduced to a lone 'A'. Fix with min-width:0 plus shorter labels, or wrap to two rows. The team-strip half of F-051 is NOT part of this: #team-strip was changed to flex-wrap:wrap in v19.5.3 (gba.css:813-822, with a comment describing this exact bug) and the evidence for that half comes from a v19.5.0 run - all six slots fit today.

backlog.title: Endurance HP where the fight is
backlog.kevin: Gabe can see how battered his team is without leaving the gym, and the heal actually looks like something happened.
acceptance: smoke: the gym stop page renders a six-slot HP strip whose values equal gymRun.hp, plus a heal control
smoke: after the heal, every slot in that strip reads full
backlog.notes: HP carrying between trainers inside a stop is a good idea that is currently invisible. renderTrainerList (gym.js:177-239) never reads gymRun at all; the only place HP is ever shown is the mid-battle switch modal (battle.js:840-874). And the heal feedback is not merely faint - it is ABSENT from this screen: pokeCenterHeal writes #gym-center-msg (gym.js:45-49), an element emitted only by renderGymList on the HUB (gym.js:156), so from inside a stop the `if (el)` guard silently no-ops. There is also no Poke Center button on the stop page, so checking on his team means leaving the stop. gymRun is junior-exempt by design (Art's team cannot faint) - the strip must therefore not appear to Art as a damage report; show it full, or not at all, in junior.

backlog.title: A shiny should look shiny everywhere
backlog.kevin: Gabe's rare black Charizard is actually black in his box and on his Pokedex page.
acceptance: smoke: with id 4 in player.shinies, the PC tile img src and the dex #poke-sprite src both resolve to the shiny sprite path without pressing SHINY
backlog.notes: Nothing is missing from the data: slimPokemon already caches front_shiny, back_shiny, official_shiny and both animated shinies (api.js:48-59). Two gaps. PIXEL_SPRITE(id) (config.js:36) has no shiny form at all, so every PC tile, sticker, team slot and favourite shelf sprite (pc.js:174, 251, 263, 384, 422) is the ordinary palette and ownership is signalled only by a corner sparkle. And the dex's SHINY chip is a manual toggle on state.isShiny (dex.js:293-325) that never consults player().shinies. Only battle.js honours shiny sprites, and only for freshly rolled wild ones. A shiny is the rarest thing a seven-year-old can own and the whole point is that it LOOKS different; right now every sparkle in his box is a promise the picture does not keep.

backlog.title: Tapping a Pokemon keeps you in the box
backlog.kevin: Tapping one of his 620 no longer throws Gabe back to the Pokedex and loses his place.
acceptance: smoke: tapping a PC tile in normal mode leaves #pc-modal visible and opens a card showing that Pokemon's own level, nickname and shiny state
smoke: closing that card restores the grid's previous scrollTop
backlog.notes: handlePCSelect (pc.js:328-344) hard-closes the modal and calls loadPoke(id), which renders the GENERIC species record - nothing on that path reads player().shinies, monLevel or nickOf, so the shiny, the level and the nickname the tile itself was showing are all dropped. He asked about HIS Charmander and got the encyclopedia article. Scroll position dies because reopening runs renderGrid, which replaces #pc-grid.innerHTML wholesale (pc.js:94); currentGen survives, scrollTop does not, and in a 620 box that scroll was the expensive part. Junior already does the right thing here - openSticker (pc.js:412-443) opens a card in place with the box still behind it - so this is 'make normal behave like junior', not new UI. The editor asked for this to be fixed alongside B-036, which is the opposite failure on the same control.

backlog.title: Take me to one I haven't got
backlog.kevin: Gabe can jump to the next Pokemon he is missing instead of guessing numbers.
acceptance: smoke: the new control lands on the lowest uncaught id above the current one and wraps at MAX_POKEMON
smoke: on a fully-caught save it does not move and does not error, and plain NEXT still steps by exactly one
backlog.notes: nav (dex.js:332-339) is pure plus-or-minus-one with wraparound, and randomPoke (327-330) is uniform over all 649 and ignores caught entirely. Ownership shows up on the dex only as the CATCH button turning into OWNED (dex.js:104-116) - there is no dimming, no gap-scanning, nothing. Gabe has 447 missing and Kanto is 100% done, so pressing NEXT anywhere in the first 151 is a guaranteed dud and his only tool is typing numbers into the search box. Rule 3: ADD the control, never replace plain NEXT with it. The uncaught-dimming grammar he is asking for already exists in the PC box (gba.css:1554-1557) and could be borrowed.

backlog.title: The E that isn't in the font
backlog.kevin: POKEDEX stops having a small stray letter in the middle of it.
acceptance: smoke: no element rendered in the pixel font has textContent matching an uppercase accented Latin capital
backlog.notes: Press Start 2P has no accented capitals, so every uppercase E-acute drops to a fallback typeface and comes back as a small lowercase letter wedged inside the capitals - in the loudest label on three of the most-visited screens. Eight live strings: index.html:99 POKEBALL, :246 SWITCH POKEMON, :435 ADD A POKEMON, :480 POKEDEX, pc.js:349, gym.js:154 POKE CENTER, battle.js:1552, explore.js:325. The boot logo is set in Courier and is fine, as is any genuine lowercase e-acute. WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT: the harness stubs the Google Fonts request with an empty stylesheet, so every screenshot in the review corpus renders in Courier - which HAS the accented capital. The same blind spot means the corpus under-reports clipping everywhere, because the real pixel font is about 40% wider. Worth pairing with B-046, which removes the stub's reason to exist.

backlog.title: Pin down Art's sticker book before someone tidies it
backlog.kevin: The screen Art understands best can't be accidentally redesigned away.
acceptance: scenes: uncaught tiles render as pure silhouettes, not greyscaled sprites
scenes: the junior dex renders no search input and no DATA button, and no string matching /junior|easy|kid|helper/i appears anywhere in a junior screen's DOM
scenes: the generation tabs are sprite images, not text labels
scenes: the lead team slot is marked by colour and position with no LEAD word, and all six slots fit on one row at 375
scenes: Art's ball drawer shows no rate, no count and no caption
backlog.notes: Four praise threads, one guard, and the regression test writes itself because the reviewers wrote it. This is the only screen that briefs Art: colour means mine, shadow means not mine yet, big green arrow means out - and he worked all three out unaided. The last assertion is the important one and it is a RULE-2 TRIPWIRE rather than a layout check: the instinct to be helpful and add a caption or a count to Art's drawer will come back, and the day it does, the accommodation starts advertising itself. junior already hides .ball-count (gba.css:637); assert it stays hidden. Also worth carrying F-084's one caveat into a follow-up: Art's gold lead tint is tan-on-cream and much quieter than Gabe's gold border.

backlog.title: Pin down the battle's wordless channel
backlog.kevin: The one screen Art can play without help stays that way.
acceptance: smoke: during turn resolution exactly one move tile is at full opacity with a highlight ring and every other battle control is dimmed and inert
smoke: every move tile carries a type glyph and its effectiveness badge is computed before the turn is committed
smoke: for a caught species the dex shows the ball glyph AND a green tick action bar; for an uncaught one, neither
backlog.notes: F-044's lockout is the best-timed thing in the game and it does two jobs: it answers 'did it hear me?' without a word, and it makes mashing harmless exactly where mashing hurts most - you cannot stack three moves into one turn and the screen never has to say no to him. Compare the dex, which has no lockout at all and goes blank under the same fingers (B-001). F-059's redundancy rule is the other one worth nailing: caught-ness is told twice, by shape AND by colour, so a pre-reader who confuses red and green still has ball-versus-tick. If a refactor ever ships an OWNED state that differs only by its text, this is the check that catches it.

backlog.title: Pin down the generous parts of the economy
backlog.kevin: The things that make coming back worth it can't quietly disappear.
acceptance: smoke: a duplicate catch still pays XP to the whole party and still says 'already in your Box'
smoke: every locked badge renders both its requirement text and a live progress fraction
smoke: every PC grid image carries loading='lazy' and the node count is unchanged across three open/close cycles on a 600+ save
smoke: with the network cut, no element contains /offline|error/i and a missing sprite resolves to the inline SVG Pokeball
backlog.notes: Four praise threads whose loss would be completely silent. F-029 is the one that matters most: when you own 620 of 649 almost everything you meet is a duplicate, and the game pays anyway, pays the whole bench, and says 'already in your Box' without sulking - that is the screen that makes a returning child feel playing is still worth doing. F-099's degradation philosophy is the other: a hand-drawn inline-SVG Pokeball rather than the web's grey broken-image icon, which would read to Art as 'you broke it'. If a future change adds a YOU ARE OFFLINE modal, this should go red. Note B-018 fixes the one path where that fallback currently fails.

backlog.title: The version number you can actually read
backlog.kevin: After a push you can tell at a glance whether the iPad got the new version.
acceptance: scenes: #boot-version measures at least 4.5:1 against the boot screen background
scenes: the Settings VERSION row is not inside the card-section labelled SOUND
backlog.notes: Measured 1.58:1 and the reviewer's arithmetic checks out: .boot-version is var(--paper-2) at opacity .75 (gba.css:1812-1815) composited over #8bac0f (main.css:11), landing at about rgb(203,205,136) on rgb(139,172,15), at 8px. At arm's length on a kitchen table 19.8.0 and 18.8.0 are indistinguishable. The Settings instance is fine on contrast but is filed between MUSIC & SOUND and BUZZ under a heading that says SOUND (index.html:400-403) - the version of the game is not a sound setting. This is the only diagnostic a non-developer has, and a stale cached shell looks exactly like a working one.

backlog.title: Don't download cries nobody can hear
backlog.kevin: The game stops spending data on sounds that are switched off.
acceptance: smoke: with pokedexos_muted=1, rendering a dex entry issues zero requests to the cries host
backlog.notes: setCry (audio.js:280-285) constructs new Audio(url) on every dex render (dex.js:255), and new Audio defaults to preload=auto, so the .ogg downloads before anyone presses CRY. Mute is consulted only at playback time (audio.js:328-330), never here. SCOPE CORRECTION that halves this thread's importance: canPlayOgg() (audio.js:266-273) already means Safari constructs no Audio object and issues no request at all - so this wastes bandwidth on Chrome and Android only, not on the boys' iPad, and the '237KB on their phones' figure in the thread is wrong. Still worth the one-line guard. Nothing about the chiptune fallback (synthCry, audio.js:300) changes.

backlog.title: The battle's words wait for its pictures
backlog.kevin: Pressing an attack lets you watch it land before the other Pokemon takes its turn.
acceptance: smoke: with PACE.fast=false, the log line for the second attacker is not written until the first attacker's .bar-ghost transition has completed (assert on a recorded timeline of logMsg timestamps against transitionend)
backlog.notes: RISKIER THAN ITS SEVERITY SUGGESTS - see the report. performAttack (battle.js:974-1028) fires updateHP and impactFx at 1006-1008 and then returns after awaitOrTap(300) at 1027, while .bar-ghost is a 300ms delay plus a 600ms transition (main.css:223) - so the enemy's line prints roughly 600ms before the bar it describes has finished draining, and the strongest feedback a child gets for pressing a button is watching his own Pokemon take damage. FOUR THINGS THAT WILL BITE: (1) awaitOrTap resolves early on tap once PACE.floor elapses, so any plain delay you add is skippable and a mashing child re-opens the gap - use the {beat:true} form (config.js:139) or the hitStop precedent in fx.js:74-80. (2) PACE.fast clamps everything to 250ms for the suite, so the test must drive it with fast off. (3) performAttack is shared by wild, gym, versus (battle.js:1942) and the switch-punish path (922) - three modes change at once. (4) Every await must stay behind the stale(e) epoch checks at 975, 982, 997 and 1005 or you resurrect the teardown race, which is the single most common source of real bugs in this file. Effort 3 and it cannot be split: the fix is one ordering rule in one function.

backlog.title: Junior buttons that show what they are about to do
backlog.kevin: Art's CRY, SHINY and RNDM buttons become pictures of their own answers.
acceptance: scenes: in junior mode the CRY, SHINY and RNDM tiles render content derived from the current species rather than a fixed category icon
backlog.notes: Two of Art's six buttons are arrows and need nothing - an arrow is a direction he already owns. The other three are a speaker, sparkles and a dice with a word underneath, and all three are abstractions that only resolve once you read the word. A dice means 'random' to someone who has played board games with a grown-up who explained probability; to Art it is a dice. Draw SHINY as this very Pokemon in its shiny colours, CRY as this Pokemon's head with sound rings, RNDM as a blurred unknown silhouette. Same six buttons, same layout, same code path - the glyphs just become specific to the thing on screen. Costs Gabe nothing; he keeps his labels. Pairs naturally with B-010, which is the same principle one row up.

backlog.title: Show Art the family
backlog.kevin: Art can see the small orange one turn into the big winged one, without a word.
acceptance: scenes: in junior mode the dex shows an evolution strip of sprites with uncaught stages greyed, and it renders without a data sheet
backlog.notes: SCOPE REDUCED SINCE FILING: v19.8.0 shipped the evolution FAN on the dex data sheet, including Eevee's whole branch with the current one ringed in gold - so Gabe's half of this wish is done. Art's is not, because junior mode has no data sheet at all (it is hidden, and smoke asserts it stays hidden). This is the one bit of Pokemon knowledge that is entirely pictures: he cannot read CHARMELEON, but he can absolutely see that the small orange one becomes the big red one becomes the enormous winged one, and that is the whole idea of evolution delivered without a single word. Grey the ones he has not caught and it doubles as a to-do list.

backlog.title: Give the small phone's bottom back to the thumb
backlog.kevin: On the little phone the buttons Art needs most sit where his hand already is.
acceptance: scenes: at 375x667 in junior mode the PC and battle entry controls sit in the lower half of the viewport and nothing overlaps the safe-area inset
backlog.notes: The only ways into the PC, the battles and the gear menu are four small chips crammed into the top-right corner - the furthest point on the phone from a four-year-old's thumb - while the bottom inch is contested by a full-width bar and a drawer that spills to the edge. Move Art's destinations down. Nothing is taken away to do it. Note this overlaps B-019 and B-021 in the same 60 pixels of screen, so schedule it after both rather than beside them - three items editing the same band at once is how a layout regression gets in.

backlog.title: Pin down the numbers that tell the truth
backlog.kevin: The counters Gabe plans his week around are guaranteed to keep saying what they mean.
acceptance: smoke: the PC generation tabs render a per-generation caught/total fraction, never one combined total
smoke: the dex header fields (number, type, height, weight, genus) all come from the API projection and match the fixture exactly
smoke: the first trainer card's printed level equals the level of the Pokemon that actually appears in that battle, and the leader is last in the roster
backlog.notes: Three praise threads about the same virtue: this game does not guess. F-009 - the gen tabs are Gabe's entire remaining job on one line, and the thing to protect is that they are PER-GENERATION; replaced by one combined total they would tell him he has work left instead of which work. F-074 - an authenticity reviewer went looking for invented stats and could not find one, right down to the genus string most fan projects paraphrase and Pikachu's habitat being forest because PokeAPI genuinely files it there; this is the layer that makes Gabe trust the game when he compares it against his cards. F-079 - the roster card promises a team and a level and then delivers exactly that, which is the reviewer's own suggested check and the cheapest of the three to write.

backlog.title: A picture lens for the ones he's proudest of
backlog.kevin: One tap fills the box with just the sparkly ones, or just the newest.
acceptance: smoke: the PC exposes NEWEST, SHINY and FAVES chips that re-filter the grid without hiding the generation tabs, and each chip renders as an icon with no required text
backlog.notes: Gabe's twelve shinies are the twelve he is proudest of and the only way to reach them is scrolling 620 cards looking for a sparkle - which happens to work today only because they sit at #001-#012; the next shiny at #430 ends that. Same for the newest catch, which files itself into dex order and vanishes at row 143, so the moment of pride has nowhere to go. Icons only, so the same control works identically in Art's book - he cannot read G1 either, and a sparkle chip that fills his screen with just the special ones is the single best thing to hand a four-year-old with 620 Pokemon. It is a LENS, not a filter that hides: nothing is removed and the gen tabs stay.

backlog.title: Fetch the next Pokemon before he asks
backlog.kevin: Pressing NEXT paints straight away instead of leaving an empty stage.
acceptance: smoke: after an entry settles, getPokemon has been called for the neighbouring ids within one second, and a NEXT tap onto a warmed neighbour renders with zero new network calls
backlog.notes: SEQUENCE THIS AFTER B-001. Prefetching on top of the current unguarded race would make out-of-order resolution MORE likely, not less - the token has to land first. There is no prefetch anywhere today: nav (dex.js:332-339) mutates state.curId and calls loadPoke, and loadPoke awaits getPokemon then getSpecies then the evolution chain serially, each with an 8s timeout. On a throttled phone profile the reviewer measured 700-1450ms per NEXT. This costs no extra data on average - those bytes were going to be fetched one tap later; it just moves the fetch into the seconds the child is already standing still. The reviewer's other suggestion is worth taking: show the already-downloaded still PNG in the spotlight until the 30KB animated one arrives.

backlog.title: Give the first minute one obvious thing to press
backlog.kevin: A brand-new save points at the first thing to do, and shows the count ticking from 0 to 1.
acceptance: smoke: on a save with zero caught, the CATCH control carries the highlight class and a caught-count element is present on the dex; both disappear after the first catch
backlog.notes: A wish, not a defect. The app already owns the trick: the explore map glows gold on one habitat and the eye goes straight to it. On a fresh save the dex is ten equally pressable buttons, nothing says the boy has caught zero, and 0/649 exists exactly once in the whole game - two taps deep behind CARD, on the card Art cannot read. Put the same glow on CATCH while caught is 0, and put a small permanent ball-and-number on the dex. First press, first GOTCHA, first digit ticks. Costs nobody anything.

backlog.title: Show my six on the fight screen
backlog.kevin: Both boys can see their whole team during a battle, and switching stops being a hidden move.
acceptance: smoke: the battle screen renders six team slots with real sprites, greyed when fainted, and tapping one opens the switch flow
scenes: the new row does not push #ball-btn or #escape-btn off screen at 375x667 in either mode
backlog.notes: The battle screen tells you everything about the opponent (LV 8 - 1/1) and nothing about your own bench. In a gym fight the route to it is a full-width SWITCH button; in a wild fight it shrinks to an unlabelled cream square with a small sprite in it (switchChipHtml, battle.js:1122-1131) - the most important control on screen when your lead is at 75/168, and the least visible. The game already draws exactly the right thing one screen earlier: the gym roster shows every trainer's team as a row of little sprites. Gabe gets his party at a glance and Art gets six pictures instead of a word. THE LAYOUT ASSERTION IS NOT OPTIONAL: the junior battle screen has overflowed 375x667 before and this adds a row to it. Versus has no switch control at all today (battle.js:1904-1922); decide deliberately whether this appears there.

backlog.title: Pack their Pokemon for the car
backlog.kevin: Before a journey the game quietly saves the pictures they actually own.
acceptance: smoke: on a warm start the worker is asked to cache the team's sprites and the four ball icons, and the request is throttled so it never runs more than N at a time
backlog.notes: Now that the worker installs (v19.8.1) the shell is safe but the pictures still are not: sprites only cache after they have been looked at, and even the four balls in the drawer are remote PNGs - so a boy scrolling to a Pokemon he has never opened gets a blank ball, and if the drawer was never opened on wifi it is four blank balls. Warm the certain things - the six on the team, the four ball icons, then everything already caught, oldest first, a few at a time so it never competes with the game. Nothing new appears on screen. SEQUENCE AFTER B-047: warming the cache while it still accepts opaque failures would poison it faster. The reviewer's second idea is worth its own line someday - a small pokeball on the boot screen, filled when the app is fully packed - because it would have shown Kevin in one glance that the worker had never installed.

backlog.title: SPARKLE stops being a slot machine
backlog.kevin: The last badge on the card is something the boys can work towards, like all the others.
acceptance: smoke: after N catches with no shiny the next encounter's shiny roll is guaranteed and the counter resets on a shiny
smoke: the SPARKLE badge's progress fraction moves as that counter climbs
backlog.notes: battle.js:302-303 is a stateless roll - 1/50, or 1/10 on the day's sparkle spot - with no counter and no floor. Every other locked badge on that card names a price the boys can pay and shows their exact distance, which is the thing F-069 praises as the best-designed part of the economy; this one cannot be made to move, and the dex has a SHINY button that shows Gabe exactly what he is not getting. It is a dice roll wearing a progress counter, aimed at a seven-year-old. Two acceptable answers and Kevin should pick: a pity floor (additive stats field, same precedent as B-044) or dropping the 0/1 so it is a surprise rather than a scoreboard. Do not lower the odds for Art or say anything about them - his roll is already the same as Gabe's and that is correct.

backlog.title: A badge for finishing a region
backlog.kevin: Finishing all 151 of Kanto is finally something the game notices.
acceptance: smoke: catching every id in a generation awards that generation's badge exactly once, it renders with a live fraction like every other locked badge, and existing badge ids are unchanged
backlog.notes: The PC box knows - the G1 tab says 151/151 - and nothing else in the game has ever mentioned it. The collection badges are 100, 300 and 649, so Gabe was last celebrated 100 Pokemon ago, the next thing is 98 away, and somewhere in that gap he completed an entire generation in silence. BADGES ARE DATA-DRIVEN and this is genuinely additive: BADGES is a plain exported array (progression.js:45-68) of {id, emoji, name, desc, check, progress}, the card renders them generically via badgeTile, and checkBadges auto-pays a Master Ball per new badge. Two cautions: badge ids are persisted in p.badges and hydrated unvalidated (state.js:164), so ids must never be reused or renamed; and there is no region concept anywhere in js/ today, so this needs its own id-range table.

backlog.title: A guest seat, so visitors stop borrowing a brother
backlog.kevin: A cousin can play without living inside Art's collection.
acceptance: smoke: the guest seat's catches and wins never touch players 1 or 2, and clearing the guest leaves both boys' saves byte-identical
backlog.notes: There are exactly two seats: the boot picker offers two cards and the gym screen offers one match. So a visiting nine-year-old has to BE Art - his Pokemon, his levels, his trainer card - and anything caught while poking about goes into a four-year-old's collection forever. A third card on WHO'S PLAYING, a pokeball with no name, a scratch save thrown away when they go home. Effort 3 and schema-touching: a third player slot has to be additive and invisible to older code, and the hydrate path validates players 1 and 2 by name (state.js:148). Ask Kevin before starting - this is the largest save-shape question in the backlog.

threads.title: I tapped fast and my Pokémon screen went empty
threads.body:
I like tapping. I tap lots and lots because tapping is the fun part.

I tapped the Pokédex a bunch of times and then the whole phone went dark blue. Just dark blue. At the very top there was a little word and some numbers, and under that nothing at all. No Pokémon. No picture. No buttons. Nothing to press.

In E-0006 and E-0007 there is only a name at the top and then the empty blue goes all the way down to the bottom of the phone. In E-0026 and E-0028 there is a tiny bit of a Pokémon squished at the top, cut off, like it was hiding behind the ceiling. In E-0005 the little row of buttons at the bottom is chopped in half so I can only see the tops of them.

I don't know how to get back. There is no green arrow here like there is in my box. I would just keep tapping the empty blue and nothing would happen, and then I would go get Dad.

My Pokémon was there and then it wasn't.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child — mashing, which is how I play, makes the Pokémon picture disappear and leaves no way back

threads.title: I pressed a Pokémon in my box and nothing happened
threads.body:
My box is full of Pokémon shapes in little squares. I pressed one.

Nothing happened.

E-0023 is before I pressed it and E-0024 is after I pressed it, and they are the exact same picture. Same squares, same shapes, same everything. Nothing got bigger, nothing lit up, nothing wiggled, no sound face, no new screen. It is like the square didn't feel me.

Everything in this box looks like a button. They are all in little white boxes with lines around them, like cards you pick up. So I press them. That is what boxes of cards are for. And when I press one and the screen does not change even a tiny bit, I think the game is broken or my finger is broken, so I press it harder, and then I press a different one, and then I stop playing.

If I press a Pokémon, please let it do SOMETHING. Get big. Jump. Sparkle. Anything so I know I did it.

threads.title: The gold star page is all words and empty grey boxes
threads.body:
There is a shiny gold star with a ribbon in the corner of my box. It is the shiniest thing on the screen so of course I pressed it.

What I got was a big cream page covered in tiny words. E-0025. I cannot read one single word of it. There is a long skinny bar at the top that is completely empty. Then twelve grey boxes with faded ghost pictures in them — a rock, a wave, a lightning, a leaf, a snowflake, a fire. All of them are grey and washed out and dim. Under each one is more little words and some numbers.

Every single box is grey. Nothing on this whole page is bright. The bar is empty. It feels like a page that is telling me I don't have any of these, twelve times in a row.

And the way out is a word in a box. Not an arrow, not a picture — a word. Downstairs in my box the way out is a big green button with an arrow on it and I know that one instantly. This one I have to guess.

The shiniest button on the screen took me somewhere with nothing for me.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes — the first thing this page shows me is an empty bar and twelve locked grey things I don't have

threads.title: My box shows me exactly which ones are mine
threads.body:
This is my favourite screen. E-0008.

I can tell what's going on without anyone reading it to me. The Pokémon I have are in COLOUR — orange Charizard with his fire, yellow Pikachu, green Bulbasaur, little orange Charmander — and they sit on bright white cards with dark lines around them. The ones I don't have yet are flat black shadows on dull grey cards. Colour means mine. Shadow means not mine yet. Nobody had to tell me that. I just knew.

My six are lined up in their own row at the top in a box of their own, so I can see my little team all together. That row makes me feel like I own something.

And the way home is a huge green button along the whole bottom with a white arrow pointing left. It is the biggest button on the screen and it is the only green thing, so I can find it every time without looking. I never get stuck in here.

Please keep this exactly like this. Colour for mine, shadow for not mine, big green arrow for out.

threads.title: I want to fill the six empty dotted holes
threads.body:
At the very top of my box there are six empty boxes made of dotted grey lines. Six holes.

In E-0023 when I had nothing, they were empty. In E-0008 I have a whole team — Charizard, Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander and two more, all right there underneath — and the six dotted holes at the top are STILL empty. Exactly the same.

Dotted empty boxes mean something goes there. That's what they mean on my sticker page and in my puzzle tray. So there are six things I am supposed to have and I don't have any of them, and I don't know what they are or how to get them, and no picture anywhere tells me.

I wish each hole had a faint little grey picture inside it showing what goes there, like a ghost of the thing, so I could go and try to get it. Or I wish I could just drag one of my colourful ones up into a hole and watch it snap in. Something I can DO.

Right now it's six empty holes at the top of my favourite screen and I don't know what I'm missing.

threads.title: NEXT walks me through Pokemon I already own
threads.body:
I have 202 out of 649. That means 447 are still missing and those are the only ones I care about. But the arrow just counts upward. The whole Saturday catch run is four screens in a row and every single one is already mine: #0025 PIKACHU, #0026 RAICHU, #0027 SANDSHREW, #0028 SANDSLASH. All four say OWNED in green. The ball drawer never opened once, because there was nothing to throw at. The harness labelled three of those steps "ball drawer" and "after the throw" and the picture never changed.

On the dex screen the only controls are the two arrows, a search box, and CRY / SHINY / RNDM / DATA / OWNED / CARD. There is nothing that says "take me to one I haven't got." Kanto is 100% done for me, so pressing NEXT anywhere in the first 151 is guaranteed to be a dud. To find my 447 I have to guess numbers into the search box.

I want a button that jumps to the next one I'm missing. Even just dimming the OWNED ones so I can see where the gaps are.

threads.title: CLOSE button chops the last row of badges in half
threads.body:
The trainer card is my to-do list. It's the one place that tells me what I still have to do. And the bottom row is cut in half by the CLOSE button.

On the champion card I can see three tiles peeking out under CLOSE: a rocket, a crown, and a grey hourglass. I cannot read what any of them want. On the mid card it's worse because I can see just enough to be teased: "Raise one to", "Become the", "Beat all 58" — three sentences with their endings sitting behind the button.

Everything above scrolls fine. ROCKO through COLLECTOR all read properly, and the locked ones even show counters like 202/300 and 202/649, which is exactly what I want. Then the list just stops mid-tile. The CLOSE button sits on top of the card instead of below it, so no matter how far I scroll, the last row is always underneath it.

Three badges I own or am chasing, and I can't read a single word of them. Same in both saves, so it isn't a one-off.

threads.title: Rematch win promises a team list then shows nothing
threads.body:
I rematched HIKER CARL and won. The victory box says, in red, "HIKER CARL DEFEATED!" and then underneath: "You caught their whole team:"

A colon. Then blank space. Then CONTINUE. Nothing is listed. There is one spoils card higher up the box (a Geodude, Lv 8, with a star and "TAP TO SEE IT!"), but it sits above the sentence that's supposed to introduce it, so the sentence reads as an empty promise. I did the fight and the reward line is a dangling colon.

The other thing: the rematch button on the gym list says REMATCH — HALF XP, so I know I'm giving something up to replay it. But this box never tells me what I actually got. There's a gold bar that fills partway and no number anywhere. Compare the wild-battle box from the same session, which says it plainly: "CHARIZARD gained 205 XP — the rest of the team got 102 each!" That one I can check. The rematch one I just have to trust.

threads.title: PC box gen tabs show exactly what is left
threads.body:
This is the best screen in the whole game for me and nothing else comes close.

One row of tabs across the PC box: G1 151/151, G2 2/100, G3 49/135, G4 0/107, G5 0/156, ALL 202/649. That is my entire remaining job on one line. I can see in one look that Kanto is finished, that Johto has barely started, that Hoenn is a third done, and that Sinnoh and Unova are completely untouched. It tells me where to go next without me having to count anything or read a paragraph.

The rest holds up too. The team strip is at the top with TAP = LEAD, my lead has a little star on it, and every box tile shows the number, the name and the level, so I can scan for holes. The green-on-green computer look is genuinely cool.

Please don't ever let those per-generation counters get replaced with one big total. The total tells me I have work left. These tell me which work.

threads.title: Give me something for finishing a whole region
threads.body:
I finished Kanto. All 151. The PC box knows — the G1 tab says 151/151. Nothing else in the game has ever mentioned it.

The trainer card's collection badges are COLLECTOR at 100, CURATOR at 300, and PROFESSOR at all 649. I'm on 202. So the last thing that celebrated me was 100 Pokemon ago, and the next thing is 98 Pokemon away, and somewhere in that gap I quietly completed an entire generation and the game said nothing at all. I only found out by opening the PC box and reading a tiny number on a tab.

I'd like a badge on the trainer card for each region I finish — KANTO, JOHTO, HOENN, SINNOH, UNOVA — five more tiles in that grid that fill in as I go. And a proper celebration the moment the last one lands, the same kind of noisy gold thing the gym wins get.

Finishing 151 of anything is the biggest thing I've done that isn't a badge. It should be a badge.

threads.seat: A child opening it for the first time
threads.title: Art's trainer card is nothing but words
threads.body:
I opened ART's save and pressed the medal. What I got (E-0025) is pixel-for-pixel the same card GABE gets (E-0057): "TRAINER CARD - ART", "POKEDEX 0/649 (0%)", the word BADGES, then twelve grey tiles each captioned "Beat LEADER ROCKO" / "0/1", and a button that says CLOSE. Junior Mode redrew the PC box into pictures and redrew the dex into big icons, but this screen it did not touch at all. For a four-year-old there is literally nothing on it. It is also the only place in the whole game that says how many you have caught, so the one screen that answers "how am I doing" is the one screen Art cannot read. Even the way out is the word CLOSE - everywhere else in Junior he gets the green BACK arrow.

Same two shots show a second thing at 375x667: the CLOSE button sits on top of the bottom badge row, slicing DRACO, VICTORY and COLLECTOR in half. Those three are the big far-away trophies - the most exciting row on the card - and they are the ones that get covered.
rule_risk: Junior Mode accessibility: the game's only progress summary is words-only, so it does not exist for a pre-reader

threads.seat: A child opening it for the first time
threads.title: Fast tapping makes the Junior dex go blank
threads.body:
Art is four. Art mashes. The harness mashed the dex arrows for him and all three frames caught the same thing: the screen is empty (E-0026, E-0027, E-0028). The top strip still shows NO. 0024 ARBOK and the type chips, and then everything from about a third of the way down is flat dark blue. No sprite, no arrows, no CATCH, no EXPLORE, no GYMS, no STICKERS - and the whole top bar with ART, the gear, PC and BTL is gone too. It stays that way across thirteen, twenty-six and thirty-nine taps, so this is not one unlucky frame mid-animation; as long as he keeps tapping, the game is a blue wall with a name floating on it.

Compare the settled Junior dex (artdex-04-dex-settled.png) - big Sandslash, six chunky buttons, a red CATCH bar the size of his thumb. That is the screen he is trying to get back to, and mashing is exactly how a four-year-old finds out what a button does. It looks like the scan/flick transition never gets a chance to finish, so each tap restarts it and the page never repaints. It does recover once he stops.

threads.seat: A child opening it for the first time
threads.title: Tapping a Pokemon in Art's PC box does nothing
threads.body:
In Art's PC box I tapped a Pokemon. The before and after screenshots (E-0023, E-0024) are byte-identical - I checked the md5, same file. Not "subtly different", not "animated frame": the game did not move a pixel.

Gabe's box does the obvious thing. He taps a tile and the PC closes and the dex jumps to that Pokemon - I tapped a silhouette and landed on CHARMANDER No. 0004 (E-0056). Art gets nothing.

This matters more for him than for Gabe, because his box is the prettiest screen in the game and it is a wall of pictures. A pre-reader's entire vocabulary for "tell me about this" is poking the picture. He pokes, nothing happens, he pokes harder, still nothing, and the lesson he learns on his first go is that the pictures are not for touching. Everything is uncaught on a fresh save, so if the rule is "Junior only opens ones you own", that means the box does nothing at all until he has caught his first one - which is the exact moment he needs it to feel alive.

threads.seat: A child opening it for the first time
threads.title: Art's empty PC box teaches the goal without a word
threads.body:
This is the best empty state in the game and it is worth protecting. Art's PC box on a save with nothing in it (E-0029, also E-0023) says everything using only pictures: six dashed empty outlines along the top that obviously want something dropped into them, a row of region tabs drawn as tiny starter sprites instead of "G1 G2 G3", a grid of pure black silhouettes that are clearly Pokemon-shaped but not yet real, and one fat green BACK arrow to get out. No numbers, no percentages, no words except his own name in the title.

A four-year-old can look at that for two seconds and know the job: fill the six boxes, turn the shadows into colours. That is the whole game explained with zero reading, and it is doing something Gabe's version of the same screen does not - his tab counters ("0/151", "0/649") are dim grey-on-green and nearly invisible (E-0055).

Please keep the dashed slots, the sprite tabs and the black silhouettes exactly as they are. If someone later "tidies" the silhouettes into greyed sprites or swaps the sprite tabs for text labels, Art loses the only screen that briefs him.

threads.seat: A child opening it for the first time
threads.title: Give the first minute one obvious thing to press
threads.body:
