Fresh save, normal mode, first screen ever (E-0058): PIKACHU No. 0025, ten buttons, and no idea which one matters. LEAD, CRY, SHINY, RNDM, DATA, CATCH, CARD, EXPLORE, GYMS all look equally pressable. Nothing says I have caught zero. Nothing says what a good day looks like. The number 0/649 exists exactly once in the game and it is two taps deep behind CARD, on the card that also happens to be unreadable for Art.

The funny part is that this app already knows how to do it. Open the explore map (/home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/normal-real-375x667-fresh/battle-01-opened-the-map.png) and one tile - DEEP FOREST - is glowing gold with sparkles while the other five sit quiet. In one glance I know where to go. That is the trick, and it is already built.

My wish: on a save with zero caught, put that same glow on CATCH, and put a tiny caught-count somewhere permanent on the dex - a pokeball and a number, no words needed. First press, first GOTCHA, first digit ticks from 0 to 1. That is a first minute with a point to it, and it costs nobody anything.

threads.seat: A 9-year-old visitor playing on someone else's save
threads.title: Versus switches Art's no-faint protection off
threads.body:
I asked the little brother for a game, so I tapped the red-and-blue GABE VS ART bar on the gym screen. Then I watched what the game actually did to him.

Gabe's side: Charizard, Lv62, 168 HP. Art's side: Pikachu, Lv9. There is no handicap and no warning. One Blaze Kick and Pikachu was gone — by the seventh pass-card the log reads ART SENT OUT CHARMANDER! and Gabe's HP bar is still completely full, 168/168, untouched. Art is going to lose every single one of his four Pokemon in a row, every single time, and he will never once land a scratch.

Everywhere else in this game Art's Pokemon can't faint. Here they can. That is the one place where the promise gets broken, and it's broken by his own brother, in the only mode the two of them are meant to play together.

If versus is the brothers' mode, it has to scale — match Art's levels to Gabe's, or cap the fight at the lower team's level.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes Art — his Pokemon faint in versus and he loses every match by design
Never take something away from a child — his team is wiped in a fight he cannot win

threads.seat: A 9-year-old visitor playing on someone else's save
threads.title: One tap on the name chip hands you the other brother's save
threads.body:
I booted the tablet, picked GABE, and got his game — champion save, Charizard Lv62, red stripe under the header. Then I tapped the little box in the top-left that says GABE, because I wanted to know what it was.

It said ART. That was the whole thing. No "are you sure", no name card, no undo. The stripe went red to blue and everything under it was a different boy's game.

Then I tapped PC and I am standing inside ART'S PC BOX with his four Pokemon and six team slots I can drag things in and out of. Nothing asked me if I was allowed to be here.

That chip is about a centimetre wide and it sits right next to the pokeball everybody taps first. Art will hit it by accident and land in Gabe's champion save with Junior Mode off — a game he can't read, where his brother's team can faint. Please make it a confirm card with both faces on it, the same one you already show at boot.
rule_risk: Saves are sacred — one accidental tap gives full edit rights over the other brother's collection with no confirm and no undo

threads.seat: A 9-year-old visitor playing on someone else's save
threads.title: PASS TO ART! is a wall of words he can't read
threads.body:
Versus is pass-and-play, so between every turn the tablet puts up a card and you're supposed to hand it over. The card says PASS TO GABE! then PASS TO ART! then PASS TO GABE! It's a heading, a sentence underneath saying no peeking at their move choice, and a button that says I'M READY.

All of it is words. The picture at the top is a grey game controller, and it is the exact same grey game controller on Art's card as on Gabe's card. Nothing on the screen changes colour between the two.

So Art, who reads nothing, gets a card that looks identical whether it's his turn or not. He can't tell if he should take the tablet or wait. When I was playing I had to read it out for him, and this game isn't supposed to need a reader.

The boot screen already solved this — it puts Charizard on Gabe's card and Pikachu on Art's. Put the same two sprites on the pass card and it works without a single word.
rule_risk: Junior Mode information carried only as words — Art cannot tell whose turn it is

threads.seat: A 9-year-old visitor playing on someone else's save
threads.title: WHO'S PLAYING? asks with faces, not names
threads.body:
This is the best screen in the whole game and I want it protected.

First boot on someone else's tablet, and before anything loads it asks WHO'S PLAYING? — two big cards, side by side. Gabe's card is a full-colour Charizard. Art's card is a Pikachu. The names sit underneath in small letters, which is exactly the right way round: the picture is the answer and the word is the caption.

I've never seen this save before and I knew instantly which one was the little brother's, because his card had the little Pokemon on it. Art can do the same thing without reading a letter — he taps his own Pikachu. And because it runs before the dex loads, he lands straight in Junior Mode instead of arriving in his brother's game and having to be rescued.

The two cards are drawn from each player's actual lead Pokemon, so they stay honest as the boys' teams change.

Please keep it sprite-first. The moment somebody "tidies" this into two text buttons, Art is locked out of choosing himself.

threads.seat: A 9-year-old visitor playing on someone else's save
threads.title: A guest seat, so visitors stop borrowing a brother
threads.body:
There are exactly two seats in this game. WHO'S PLAYING? offers two cards. The gym screen offers one match: GABE VS ART — and before anyone types a name it literally reads GABE VS P2.

Which means when I come round, I have nowhere to sit. To play versus against Gabe I have to be Art: his Pokemon, his levels, his team. If I win, the win goes onto Art's trainer card as his versus win, not mine. If I catch something while I'm poking about, it goes into his collection forever and he didn't catch it. I am wearing a four-year-old's game like a borrowed coat, and I can't put anything back.

What I'd love is a third card on the WHO'S PLAYING screen — a pokeball, no name needed — that gets a scratch save. Let the visitor pick six of the host's Pokemon to borrow for one match, keep their own score, and throw the whole thing away when they go home.

Then nobody has to touch a brother's save to have a fight.

threads.seat: A four-year-old with a very fast finger
threads.title: Mashing the dex leaves a huge empty screen with no way out
threads.body:
I tapped the dex fast, the way Art does, and the game got stuck showing me almost nothing. Three shots in a row — 13 taps, 26 taps, 39 taps — and every one is the same: a name and two type tiles squeezed into the top fifth of the phone, a sprite that never finished fading in, and then a dead navy-blue rectangle filling the other four fifths. No grid. No sprites. No BACK arrow. Nothing to touch.

The champion save does the exact same thing at the exact same taps, so this isn't one unlucky frame — mashing puts the dex detail into a state where it just stops drawing the rest of itself.

For me that screen is over. There is no picture on it. I can't read ARBOK, so all I see is a big blue nothing where my Pokemon used to be, and no arrow to press. I'd hand the phone to Dad. When the mashing stopped I wasn't even on the dex any more — I'd landed in the PC box (E-0047).

threads.seat: A four-year-old with a very fast finger
threads.title: The ball drawer's only exit is a word: CANCEL
threads.body:
I pressed the big red BALL button and a card slid up over the whole battle. Four white rows: POKEBALL, GREAT BALL, ULTRA BALL, MASTER BALL. Then the biggest, brightest, bottom-most thing on the card — a wide red bar that says CANCEL.

The ball rows are fine, they have ball pictures and I can tell the red one from the blue one from the purple one. But CANCEL is text only. No arrow, no X, no picture at all. It is also the single most mash-attractive target in the modal: bottom of the screen, saturated red, full width, right under my thumb.

So the two things I will hit most are the one thing I can't read and the one thing that throws away the Pokemon. Same modal in both saves — the shiny Pidgey one hurt.

Everywhere else this app knows how to do it: the PC box exit is a green bar with a proper left-arrow sprite on it (E-0047). This card should have that arrow.
rule_risk: Junior Mode: the only way out of the catch modal is a written word, so a pre-reader cannot back out of it

threads.seat: A four-year-old with a very fast finger
threads.title: PC card has no close button, and a star sits where close should be
threads.body:
I tapped a Charmander in my box and got a lovely big card. Then I wanted out. There is nothing to press. No X, no arrow, no bar. The PC's own green BACK bar is still there but it's dimmed out behind the dark scrim, so it reads as switched off. The only exit is tapping the dark part outside the card, which nobody told me.

Worse: there IS a thing in the top-right corner, notched into the card exactly where a close button lives on every other app in the world — and it's a white star. So the corner I aim at to leave is actually the favourite toggle. A fast finger going for "close" flips favourites instead, and mashing it flips them on and off with no picture change big enough for me to notice I did anything.

Both saves, same card. The card itself is great; it's the getting-out that traps me.

threads.seat: A four-year-old with a very fast finger
threads.title: The battle move buttons are perfect for a kid who can't read
threads.body:
This is the best screen in the game for me and please never change it.

Four huge buttons, two by two, each one filling a quarter of the bottom of the phone. Not a single letter on any of them. A flame on orange. A feather on blue. A fist on grey. A mountain on tan. The colour tells me the type and the picture tells me the move, and I don't need either explained.

Underneath each one there are little square pips that fill in and empty out, so I can see a move getting used up without anyone writing a number at me. And when a move is bad the button tells me in pictures too: against Hiker Carl's Geodude all four got a little orange double-down arrow, and against the shiny Pidgey the mountain move got a grey X. I knew not to press it.

They're also big enough that my fast finger actually lands where I aimed — I never mis-hit one across four battle shots. Every other screen should copy this.

threads.seat: A four-year-old with a very fast finger
threads.title: Give me one BACK arrow, same corner, on every screen
threads.body:
I counted how to get out of things across my shots and the answer is different every single time.

Battle: small arrow, top left. Gym: bigger arrow, top left, but lower down. PC box: green bar with an arrow, across the bottom. Trainer card: a white bar that says CLOSE, floating over the badges it's covering. Ball drawer: a red bar that says CANCEL. Pokemon card in the PC: nothing. Mashed dex: nothing.

Seven screens, five different escapes, two dead ends. I can't read, so every new shape is a new thing to learn, and when I'm mashing I don't learn — I just want the one place I always press to go back.

I wish there was a single arrow button, always the same sprite, always the same corner, always drawn on top of whatever is open, on every screen including the ones that currently have none. Then no amount of my tapping can strand me, and Dad doesn't have to come rescue the phone.

threads.seat: A boy back after three weeks away
threads.title: Gym victory promises a list, then shows nothing
threads.body:
I came back with 620 caught and beat HIKER CARL for the rematch. The ceremony (E-0143) gives me a trophy, one Geodude card, an XP bar — then a red line "HIKER CARL DEFEATED!", then "You caught their whole team:" — and then nothing at all. Blank paper, then CONTINUE. A colon with no list under it.

I think I know why: I already own every one of Carl's Pokemon, so the spoils grid has nothing new to put there. But the sentence still gets printed. To me it reads like the game forgot to give me my prize.

What makes this sting is that ten steps earlier, in the same session, the WILD catch handled the exact same situation perfectly (E-0131): "EKANS was caught (already in your Box). CHARIZARD gained 179 XP." That screen knew I already had it and said so warmly. The gym screen doesn't. Either drop the caption when the grid is empty, or say what the wild screen says: already in your Box, here's the XP anyway.

threads.seat: A boy back after three weeks away
threads.title: Art's box opens on six empty holes
threads.body:
This is the one that would actually upset my little brother. He owns 620 Pokemon. He taps PC, and the very first thing at the top of ART'S PC BOX is six empty grey dashed rectangles (E-0030, still empty after 39 taps of mashing in E-0036). Directly underneath them sits his real team — Charizard with a star, Pikachu, Blastoise, Snorlax, Gyarados, Dragonite — full colour, full sprites.

I'm fairly sure the dashed row is a favourites shelf, because tapping a Pokemon opens a card with a big hollow star in the corner (E-0031). But nothing on screen says that. There is no icon in the empty slots, no star ghost, nothing. To a boy who cannot read a single word and has been away three weeks, the top shelf of his collection is six holes where something used to be.

Put a faint grey star inside each empty slot so the shape itself explains the shelf, or don't draw the shelf at all until he stars his first one.
rule_risk: Junior Mode never punishes — an unexplained empty shelf reads as loss to a pre-reader

threads.seat: A boy back after three weeks away
threads.title: The numbers I came back for are the faintest text
threads.body:
After three weeks the first question is "how far did I get?" Every answer to that is a number, and numbers are styled paler than the words next to them everywhere in the app.

Gym Circuit (E-0135): "TRAINERS DEFEATED:" is bright amber. The "40/58" beside it is dim grey on dark navy and I genuinely had to lean in. Same screen, the versus bar reads "GABE VS P 2" with the 2 nearly gone.

PC box (E-0110): every card says "Lv 5 5" with the digits a washed-out grey-green on dark green. The generation tabs — my main way through 620 Pokemon — show "1 0 0 / 1 0 0", "1 2 7 / 1 5 6" so faintly they look disabled.

Trainer card (E-0112): "620/649 (96%)" is the proudest fact I own and it's the palest thing on the card.

On cream backgrounds it's fine. On the dark screens it fails. The label survives and the value dies, which is backwards — the value is the part I came back to read.

threads.seat: A boy back after three weeks away
threads.title: A duplicate catch still pays, and says so kindly
threads.body:
This is the thing that made coming back feel fine instead of pointless, and I want it protected.

When you own 620 of 649, almost everything you meet is something you already have. I threw a ball at a wild EKANS I definitely already owned. The game gave me the full ceremony anyway (E-0131): the Ekans sprite, a huge green tick, a gold XP bar filling, "VICTORY!" in red with stars — and then, plainly and without any sulking, "EKANS was caught (already in your Box). CHARIZARD gained 179 XP — the rest of the team got 89 each!"

No "you wasted a ball." No greyed-out nothing. It told me the truth and still paid me, and it paid my whole bench, not just my lead. That is exactly what a kid who's been away needs — proof that playing is still worth doing even when the dex is nearly finished.

Please keep the tick, keep the XP bar animating, and keep the "already in your Box" wording. If a future change ever makes a duplicate silent or XP-free, this is the screen that broke.

threads.seat: A boy back after three weeks away
threads.title: Fill the empty shelf with my last six catches
threads.body:
Nothing punished me for being gone — no broken streak, no lost Pokemon, my quests just sat at 0/3 waiting (E-0145). Thank you for that. But nothing welcomed me either. I opened the app and it was exactly as blank as if I'd closed it a second ago.

Here's a wish that costs nothing and takes nothing away. Those six empty dashed slots at the top of the PC box (E-0030, E-0110) — when a boy has starred nothing, fill them instead with the last six Pokemon he caught, newest first, as sprites only. No words, no dates, no "you've been away 21 days," no guilt.

Art opens his box and the top shelf shows the six he was excited about three weeks ago, in colour. He can't read, but he'll remember those six. I'd get the same thing on the dex side — my lead Pokemon doing its idle bounce and its cry on first open of the day.

It turns the emptiest thing on the screen into the warmest, and it only ever adds.

threads.title: The É in POKÉ breaks out of the pixel font
threads.body:
Press Start 2P has no accented capitals. So every time the game writes its own brand word in caps, the É drops through to a fallback typeface and comes back as a small lowercase é wedged inside the capitals: POKéDEX on the trainer card, POKéBALL in the ball drawer, POKé CENTER on the gym screen. It reads like a typo in the middle of the loudest label on each screen, and it is on three of the most-visited screens in the game.

Why nobody has caught it: the playtest harness stubs the Google Fonts request with an empty stylesheet, so every screenshot in this review corpus is rendered in the Courier fallback — and Courier HAS an É, so the corpus shows a clean POKÉDEX (E-0072, E-0065, E-0096). I re-ran the same screens with the font actually loading and the break is there every time. Worth knowing generally: the review shots are ~40% narrower than the real thing, so they under-report clipping everywhere.

Fix is one word long: write POKEDEX / POKEBALL / POKE CENTER, or keep the accent only in mixed case (Pokémon in the dex footer is fine — that é is a real lowercase é).

threads.title: The trainer card has only two text sizes, one is the floor
threads.body:
I measured every string on Gabe's champion card. There is a 13px title, and then literally everything else is 8px — the section labels, the 202/649 count, each badge's NAME, each badge's how-to-earn caption, each 0/1 progress line. Nothing is bigger than anything else, so the eye has nowhere to land on a screen that exists purely to say WELL DONE.

Two consequences. The badge name ROCKO and the instruction "Beat LEADER ROCKO" are the same weight and size, so the reward and the homework look identical. And the captions are mixed-case sentences, which CLAUDE.md already says the pixel font can't carry: at 375 with the real font "Beat LEADER ROCKO" becomes a three-line ragged stack inside a 100px box, and VICTORY's "Beat Victory Road & the Elite 4" is seven words in a font designed for three.

What I'd do: badge name at 11-12px, drop the caption entirely on badges he has already earned (he knows how he got it), and keep the caption only on locked ones as ≤4 uppercase words. That alone shortens the grid enough to stop it hiding under CLOSE (F-007).

threads.title: Ball drawer's last column touches the edge, count orphans
threads.body:
On the 375 phone the ball drawer's fourth column has no gutter at all. MASTER BALL and its 100% CATCH line end one pixel from the right edge of the screen — the type is not clipped, but it is kissing the bezel, and on any phone with a rounded corner or a case lip it will look cut.

Worse, the master ball is the only ball with a count, so "X1" wraps onto a fourth line all by itself, hanging below the other three columns and sitting right on the bottom edge of the drawer. Three tidy two-line stacks and then one lopsided four-line one. It reads as a rendering accident rather than as "you own one of these".

Both the corpus shot and my real-font re-run show it, so it isn't a fallback-font artefact — the real pixel font is wider, so it's marginally tighter in real life.

Cheapest fix: put the count inline on the name row (MASTER BALL X1) or as a small badge on the ball sprite, and give the drawer 8px of side padding so no column ever runs to the screen edge.

threads.title: The dex button grid never wraps, never truncates
threads.body:
This is the best-set screen in the game and it should be locked down. Nine buttons — LEAD, CRY, SHINY, RNDM, DATA, CATCH, CARD, EXPLORE, GYMS — and every single label is one uppercase word of seven characters or fewer, each sat under its own icon. On the small 375 phone, with the real pixel font loaded (which is about 40% wider than the fallback the test shots use), not one of them wraps, truncates, shrinks or collides with its neighbour. That is not luck; the vocabulary was chosen to fit.

The hierarchy above it is just as disciplined: NO. 0025 at 9px and grey, PIKACHU at 20px and white with a hard drop shadow, the ELECTRIC chip at 8px. Three sizes, three jobs, and a 7-year-old's eye goes to the name first every time.

As a regression test: at 375 wide with Press Start 2P loaded, every .tool-btn label must stay on one line at its authored size. Any future button called COLLECTION or FAVOURITES breaks it — the rule to keep is one word, ≤7 characters.

threads.title: Three balls, one caption — say what's different instead
threads.body:
In the battle's THROW A BALL modal, three of the four rows carry the exact same green caption: POKÉBALL — BETTER WHEN WEAKENED, GREAT BALL — BETTER WHEN WEAKENED, ULTRA BALL — BETTER WHEN WEAKENED. Twelve words that never change between choices, so they add three lines of noise and zero information: the one thing Gabe is trying to decide — which ball is stronger — is the thing the text refuses to tell him.

The dex's own ball drawer already gets this right two taps away: 1x RATE, 1.5x RATE, 2x RATE, 100% CATCH. The same four rows, ranked, in fewer characters.

Wish: make the modal's caption the differentiator (1x / 1.5x / 2x / NEVER FAILS) and put the shared advice in the header line that's already there. And for Art, who reads none of it, carry the same ranking as one, two, three filled pips beside each ball so the ladder is visible as shape rather than as words — same drawer, same order, no reading required, and no note that anything has been made easier for him.

threads.title: Art's two Normal moves are the same picture twice
threads.body:
Following on from the praise for these buttons — they are the right idea, and that is exactly why this hurts.

I opened Art's battle against a wild Togekiss (E-0014) and looked at his four choices as a four-year-old would: an orange flame, a grey fist, a blue feather, a grey fist. Two of his four buttons carry the identical yellow fist on the identical grey. I sampled the pixels: the two greys are rgb(203,207,200) and rgb(208,211,204) — a contrast ratio of 1.04:1 between them. They are the same colour. The only difference is faint diagonal hatching and one extra pip.

The cause is that the button is coloured by TYPE, not by move, so any Pokémon knowing two Normal moves gets two identical buttons. Charizard here knows two. The same collision appears in Gabe's game, where STRENGTH and SECRET POWER are twins (E-0142) — but Gabe can read the words underneath and Art cannot. For Art those two buttons are one button that sometimes does something different.

I also measured the grey against the cream panel behind it: 1.35:1. The buttons barely separate from their own background.

threads.title: White words on the yellow ELECTRIC tile, 1.34 to 1
threads.body:
I opened the dex on Pikachu (E-0113) and looked at the type tile under his name. The word ELECTRIC is white text on the electric-yellow chip. I sampled it: text rgb(244,239,207) on tile rgb(232,208,52). That is a contrast ratio of 1.34:1. The accepted floor for text this size is 4.5:1. It is not dim — it is nearly invisible, and the word only resolves at all because the pixel font has a hairline shadow.

I checked whether it was a one-off. Two Pokémon later (E-0119) the GROUND tile is white on tan at 2.30:1. Same failure, less extreme.

The pattern is that every type tile paints white text on the type's own colour, which works fine for the dark types (poison purple, dragon indigo) and collapses on every pale one — electric, ground, ice, fairy, normal. On a phone screen in a sunlit kitchen the yellow tile is a blank yellow rectangle.

This is the one place in the app that names a Pokémon's type in words, and Gabe reads it on every single dex entry.

threads.title: Green Pokemon disappear into Gabe's green PC box
threads.body:
I opened Gabe's PC box on the hoarder save (E-0110, again at E-0137) and scrolled the first page of the grid. Every card is a dark green panel on a dark green screen. The orange and blue Pokémon — Charmander, Charizard, Blastoise, Wartortle — jump straight off it. The green ones do not.

I zoomed in and sampled. Caterpie's body against its own card is 2.38:1. Bulbasaur is 2.07:1. Metapod, #011, is a pale green blob on dark green and I genuinely had to look twice to confirm a sprite was there at all. Charmander on the same card colour reads at a glance, not because his luminance is better (2.95:1, barely different) but because orange against green is a hue apart. The green ones have neither.

So the box is a colour-sorted wall where roughly a fifth of the collection — every Grass and most Bug — is camouflaged. For a boy scrolling 649 slots looking for the one he just caught, that is the worst possible place to hide a Pokémon. In Art's cream box (E-0016) the same sprites read fine, which is the tell: it is the green card, not the sprites.

threads.title: The badge wall is twelve colours a pre-reader can read
threads.body:
I opened the Gym Circuit on Art's champion save (E-0009) and zoomed the badge grid, and it is the best-coloured surface in the whole app.

Twelve badges, and every one is a different hue AND a different silhouette: grey rock, blue wave, yellow bolt, green leaf, purple orb, red glove, white ghost, ice crystal, orange flame, green dragon, snow peak, gold crown. Nothing relies on a word. Art can point at the fire one. The cream tile and gold frame give each icon a consistent surround so the hues read against a fixed backdrop instead of against each other, and the green tick sits in the same corner of every tile — one state colour, one position, twelve times. That is a real visual language and he owns it without reading a letter.

Please keep this exact treatment if the badge screen is ever reworked: distinct hue plus distinct shape plus a fixed-corner state mark. If anything is worth a nudge, it is that ghost, ice and mountain are the three pale icons on a pale tile — a slightly warmer tile behind just those three would let all twelve land equally.

threads.title: Let type colour mean the same thing on every screen
threads.body:
The battle screen already proves this works. In E-0014 the fire move is orange and the flying move is sky blue, and Art picks the orange one without reading. The type palette exists, it is good, and it is used in exactly one place.

Everywhere else colour carries no meaning. Gabe's PC box (E-0110) paints all 649 cards the same green. Art's box (E-0016) paints them all the same cream. The dex type tile (E-0113) does use the type colour but hides the word in white on top of it. So a boy who has learnt orange-means-fire in battle gets nothing for that knowledge the moment he leaves it.

What I want: the same type hue on the PC card, the dex card frame and the team strip. Fire cards warm, water cards blue, grass cards a green that is not the box's own green. Art gets a box he can sort by colour instead of by name — he can find all his fire ones with a finger. Gabe gets a 649-slot grid he can scan by hue.

One palette, four screens, no new words.

threads.title: The battle text is one beat ahead of the picture
threads.body:
I pressed BLAZE KICK and looked at what the screen actually shows a moment later (E-0157). The log has already moved on to "KAKUNA USED BUG BITE!" — but the -34 from MY hit is still floating and fading over Kakuna, and Charizard's bar still reads a full 86/86. Two turns are on screen at once, and the one the words describe is the one you can't see yet. Junior at 375 (E-0042) has the same collision from the other side: the log says "PIDGEY USED WING ATTACK!" while a -14 pops over Art's Charizard, so the only fresh motion on his screen is his own Pokemon getting hit — his hit landed and vanished before the frame.

What I expected: my move lands, I get a held beat to enjoy it (flash, number, the enemy bar visibly draining), THEN the opponent moves and my bar drains. One thing at a time. Right now the text timer and the sprite/bar timers run independently and overlap, so the strongest feedback a kid gets for pressing a button is watching his own guy take damage.

threads.title: Every dex landing catches the sprite half-drawn
threads.body:
Normal mode, 390 wide, one deliberate tap on a Pokemon in the PC box (E-0153). What I got was CHARMANDER rendered as a torn vertical sliver — maybe 40% of him, in ragged strips, with a soft orange blob where the rest should be. It reads as a broken image, not a reveal.

This is not a one-off from a fast finger. Three separate dex landings in my slice, three half-drawn sprites: E-0153 after a single tap, and E-0044 (ARBOK) and E-0046 (FEAROW) in Junior at 375, both ghosted behind a teal scan line with the headline text double-imaged. I never once saw a finished sprite on a dex screen.

What I expected: the reveal to be over by the time the screen settles, or to be short and clean enough that its middle frame still looks like a Pokemon. Whatever wipe is running is slow enough to be the thing you actually see. Gabe taps NEXT dozens of times a session; a shredded Charmander on every one of them is a lot of glitch for very little ceremony.

threads.title: Rematch ceremony is longer than the rematch
threads.body:
I went back into Boulder Gym on the mid save. The header says 5/5 DEFEATED and every trainer has a green tick and a REMATCH — HALF XP button (E-0150). I pressed one and got HIKER CARL's quote card, then the fight: a single Lv8 Geodude, 1/1, against a Lv30 Charizard at full 86/86 (E-0151).

That is four screens of build-up — circuit, gym list, trainer quote, battle intro — wrapped around a fight that cannot last more than one tap and cannot be lost. The pacing curve is upside down: the slow part is the part with no stakes, and the payoff is half XP.

What I expected: either the rematch scales to my team so the ceremony is earned, or the ceremony gets out of the way — tap REMATCH, go straight into the fight, no quote card. Right now the Gym Circuit's replay value is mostly loading screens, and it's the screen Gabe returns to most once he's cleared a region.

threads.title: The battle locks itself while the turn plays out
threads.body:
This is the best-timed thing in the game and I want it nailed down before someone refactors it away.

The instant a move is chosen, the tile you pressed keeps a bright gold ring and stays at full colour, and everything else — the other three moves, the red BALL bar, even the BACK arrow — fades to about 40%. E-0157 in normal at 390, E-0042 in Junior at 375: identical behaviour, both sizes, both modes.

Two things this buys. First, it answers "did it hear me?" without a single word, which is the whole ballgame for Art: the button he touched is the one thing still lit. Second, it makes mashing harmless exactly where mashing hurts most — you cannot stack three moves into one turn, and the screen never has to say no to him. Compare the dex, which has no lockout at all and goes blank under the same fingers.

Worth a regression test: during turn resolution, exactly one move tile is at full opacity with a highlight ring and every other battle control is visibly dimmed and inert.

threads.title: Let a shiny stop the clock
threads.body:
A shiny Pidgey turned up for Art (E-0041) — the golden palette, the sparkles in the name plate, "WOW! A SHINY PIDGEY APPEARED!!" across the log. It's a genuinely rare, genuinely lovely moment. And then the next thing that happens is Pidgey attacks him (E-0042). The whole celebration is a line of text he cannot read, and it is gone before he has finished noticing the bird is the wrong colour.

What I want: when something rare shows up, stop everything. No enemy turn, no timer, nothing to lose. Freeze the battle, pulse the sprite, throw sparkles across it, play its cry, and just sit there until he taps. Then the fight starts. Give the moment a beat of its own instead of letting the turn loop roll straight over it.

The same held beat would suit a level-up or a new evolution. The game already knows how to dim everything and wait — the battle does it every turn. Point that same trick at the moments worth remembering, and Art gets to feel lucky instead of just getting pecked.

threads.title: Wild Pokémon usually arrive with no voice at all
threads.body: E-0002 is the moment I care about most in this whole game. Art is looking at a cactus he has never seen, and the only thing in the room that says what it is, is the line WILD MARACTUS APPEARED! — words he cannot read. So I ran the game unmuted and tagged every oscillator by which bus it came out of. In a 24-second junior session (junior-390-wild.png) the cry bus fired exactly twice: once on boot, once when I pressed CRY. Nothing when the wild Pokémon appeared. Across four wild encounters in three sessions, only one Pokémon made a sound as it arrived — a Kakuna came in silent and the Piplup after it got a voice, so it is not consistently missing, it is a coin flip, most likely racing the species fetch. The cries themselves are lovely. They just only exist on the Pokédex screen. The one place a voice would do the most work — a creature appearing in front of a boy who cannot read its name — is the place it usually does not happen.
rule_risk: Junior Mode information contract: at the encounter, who just showed up exists only as words, which for Art means it does not exist

threads.title: One tap silences the whole house, for both brothers, forever
threads.body: The sound chip sits in the top bar of every screen, one thumb-width from the gear, with no label. I tapped it once as GABE: sound off. I closed the app and reopened it as ART: still off. Mute lives in one global key, so it is not Gabe's setting or Art's, it is the house's, and it survives restarts and player switches. Now look at what Art has to work out from: junior-375-unmuted.png (on) and art-inherits-mute-375.png (off). Same chip, same little grey speaker, same size. The only difference is a red ring about ten pixels across — smaller than the CRY icon eight rows below it, which is drawn three times larger. For a four-year-old the game just went quiet and the sign explaining why is tinier than the thing he was reaching for. The mute machinery underneath is honest work: with sound off, pressing CRY books zero notes, not volume-zero notes. The problem is only that it is one silent, unconfirmed, shared, sticky tap away, and the boy who most depends on sound is the one who cannot read his way back out.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child: one accidental tap removes the entire non-verbal feedback channel from a pre-reader, across sessions and across brothers, with no readable way back

threads.title: Every screenshot in this review was taken with sound off
threads.body: Look at the header chip in E-0048, in normal-real/dex-05-pressed-CRY.png, in junior-real/dex-05-pressed-CRY.png, and in zoom2-header.png. The little speaker has a red slash through it in all of them. The harness sets the mute flag before every single run, so all five save profiles, both modes, both phone sizes and every scenario played out in total silence. E-0050 is a gym battle with a music track nobody has ever heard. That is the entire audio surface — the chiptune, the sound effects, the cry fallback, and the mix between the three of them — sitting at zero coverage, in an app where for a pre-reader roughly half the meaning is carried by sound. It is also why the two issues above have never surfaced in any report: nobody was listening. This is the cheapest thing on my list to fix. Run the existing scenarios once with mute off and count cry-bus events per encounter and per catch, exactly the way I did here. One unmuted pass turns audio from an untested surface into a tested one.

threads.title: The 404 cries never leave a silence, and nothing ever talks
threads.body: Worth saying loudly, because 31 machine threads are this same 404 and they all read like something is broken. Nothing is broken. The .ogg cry is unplayable on the boys' phones anyway, and the game already knows — it checks the format first, and when a real cry cannot be had it builds one. I tapped CRY and the first note landed 73 milliseconds later: three triangle notes on their own cry bus, shaped by that species' own stats, and identical every single time I pressed it. Pikachu sounds like Pikachu, not like a generic beep, and he will sound the same tomorrow, which for a four-year-old is the whole difference between a voice and a noise. The mute is honest too: with sound off, CRY booked zero oscillators — not silent-but-playing, genuinely not played. And the thing I was asked to check positively: across every session I ran — boot, dex, catching, exploring, wild battles, attacks, mute toggles, reloads, both brothers — speechSynthesis.speak was never called and no utterance was ever constructed. Not once. Please keep all three.

threads.title: Let the caught Pokémon shout when the ball opens
threads.body: Art threw a ball at a Nidoqueen and caught her. Between the throw and the OWNED screen I logged every note the game played: a wobble tick, a wobble tick, a wobble tick, a rising two-note jingle, and the background music underneath. Five seconds of the biggest moment in his whole game, and the cry bus never fired once. The new Pokémon never made a sound. She already has a voice — the dex plays it 73ms after a tap, from data the game has already cached. I want that voice at the moment the ball clicks shut, when a wild one appears, and when Art sends his own out. That is exactly how the real games teach a small child which creature is which: the picture and the noise arrive together and stick together. Right now Art gets the picture and a sentence he cannot read. Give him the noise and the catch becomes something Kevin can hear from the next room — he will know it went well without being told.

threads.title: On the small phone my team is only four and a half
threads.body:
I opened the PC box on the 375-wide phone and the TEAM strip across the top shows Charizard, Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander... and then Geodude sliced down the middle by the right edge of the screen. Slot six is not on screen at all. I only knew it was there because the cropped shot of the strip itself shows all six.

The strip does slide sideways, but nothing says so: no arrow, no shadow, no half-hidden card that reads as "keep going". The five and a half cards sit inside a neat green box with a closed border, which is the universal signal for "this is all of it".

That strip is also the only way to set your lead — the label literally says TAP = LEAD. So on the smallest phone Gabe can't choose two of his six Pokemon as his lead without discovering an invisible swipe. On my 667-tall screen there is plenty of vertical room going spare; two rows of three would fit and end the problem.

threads.title: The Master Ball count falls off the bottom of the screen
threads.body:
I tapped CATCH on the dex screen and the ball drawer slid up from the bottom. Four balls, big lovely sprites, fine. But the fourth one is the Master Ball, and on a 375x667 screen its label needs two lines — MASTER BALL / 100% CATCH — which pushes the bit that actually matters, the "X 1" count, onto a third line that ends about ten pixels from the bottom edge of the viewport.

That is the worst place on this phone to put anything. On a real iPhone SE in Safari that band is where the browser's own toolbar lives, and in the home-screen app it's the swipe-up bar. So the one number a kid checks before spending his rarest item — how many have I got left? — is the number sitting under the browser chrome and under his thumb.

The other three balls are single-line and sit comfortably. It's only the Master Ball, and only at 375, and it's the only one where the count is the point.

threads.title: CANCEL is white text on a cream button
threads.body:
Mid-battle I opened THROW A BALL and then SWITCH POKEMON. Both panels end with a big bordered button at the bottom, and both times the word inside it is rendered in near-white on the cream notepaper background. I can just about make out CANCEL if I know it's there; on a bright phone in a car, nobody will. Every other label on the same panel — POKEBALL, BETTER WHEN WEAKENED, the level numbers — is dark navy and perfectly crisp, so this one button is the odd one out.

The button is large and it does work, so a kid who taps the empty-looking box discovers the exit by accident. But mid-battle the visible options are four attack cards and one blank rectangle, and a blank rectangle reads as "broken", not "back out".

This is the normal-mode sibling of F-022 (which is about Art not being able to read the word at all). Here Gabe can read fine — he just can't see it. Same button, two different children stuck on it.

threads.title: The dex home screen is flawless on the small phone
threads.body:
This is the screen I expected to break first and it is the best-behaved thing in my whole slice. At 375x667 the dex fits: header, number, big name, type tags, a sprite with room to breathe, the search row, then twelve buttons in a tidy grid — and not one pixel of horizontal overflow, no clipped label, no text squeezed to five pixels.

The hierarchy survives the shrink too. CATCH is a full-width red bar planted right in the middle of the button block, which on a 667-tall phone lands exactly under a thumb, and EXPLORE and GYMS are colour-coded slabs below it. Every small tile carries its icon above the word, so LEAD / CRY / SHINY / RNDM still parse when you can't read them. The tiles are roughly 72 by 60 CSS pixels, comfortably over the tap-target minimum, with real gutters — I never mis-hit one.

Whoever sized this grid did it on a small phone, not a laptop window. Please don't let a future row of buttons quietly push CATCH off the thumb line.

threads.title: Give the bottom of the small screen back to the phone
threads.body:
Two things fight over the last inch of a 667-tall screen. The PC box's CLOSE PC bar (and Art's green BACK bar) is a solid slab pinned to the bottom that sits directly on top of a whole row of Pokemon cards — in the fresh save the fourth row's names are completely under it, and in Art's box the same row is buried under the green. And the ball drawer spills its last line to the very edge. Meanwhile the only ways into the PC, the battles and the gear menu are four small chips crammed into the top-right corner, the furthest point on the phone from a four-year-old's thumb.

My wish: on short screens, leave a clear strip at the bottom that content scrolls past rather than under, and move the PC / BTL chips down into it as big icon buttons. Art gets his destinations where his hand already is, Gabe stops losing a row of his collection behind a green bar, and nothing has to be taken away to do it.

threads.title: Art's type tile is a word, but the game owns a picture for it
threads.body:
On the dex screen — the screen Art lives on — the type sits in a coloured tile that says POISON (E-0033) or NORMAL / FLYING (E-0035). Right beside it, in an identical-sized tile, the habitat is a picture: a tree, a wheat stalk, a cave mouth. So the row reads: word, word, picture. Art can decode the third tile and not the first two.

What makes this sting is that the picture already exists. Open any Pokemon in his PC box and the type comes back as a flame on orange, no word at all (E-0031). Somebody sat down and drew a whole type alphabet — and thought hard about it too; the NORMAL glyph is a fist and not a star, precisely so a four-year-old wouldn't read it as 'the special one'. That alphabet is used on the card and on the battle buttons, then abandoned on the one screen he taps most.

The two tiles in E-0035 are the same size, same shape, same border. One is a picture and one is a label. To Art the difference is that half his Pokemon's identity is simply missing. Put the glyph in the tile — keep the word next to it for Gabe if you like, but lead with the picture.

threads.title: The top-bar sound button is just a red NO sign
threads.body:
I zoomed the header in Art's dex screen (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-kevin-pokedex/c02990b7-8698-403c-8544-c2332c13aa8b/scratchpad/hdr.png, cropped from the shot I generated at /home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/junior-real-375x667-hoarder/artdex-04-dex-settled.png). With sound off, the button is a big red prohibition circle with a small dark-grey speaker almost invisible underneath it. What a four-year-old sees is the NO sign — the one on road signs and 'do not touch' stickers. It is the second-most prominent thing in his top bar and it appears to mean 'you are not allowed'.

With sound on it becomes a plain speaker with sound waves — which is the exact same glyph as the CRY button four rows down in his own toolbar, visible in the same screenshot. So one speaker plays a Pokemon's voice and an identical speaker kills every sound in the game.

This one matters more than a normal mislabel. The game deliberately never talks, so cries, beeps and the chiptune are the whole non-visual channel. One curious tap in the corner takes all of it away, and the button that gives it back is now a NO sign that looks like the thing that caused the problem. Make the off state a picture of silence he can read — the speaker at full size with a single red slash, or better, the music note fading out — and give the CRY button a different glyph entirely, e.g. the Pokemon's own head with sound rings.
rule_risk: Never take something away from a child — one unlabelled tap removes Art's entire sound channel and nothing in the picture tells him how to get it back.

threads.title: Five starters and a book: the ALL tab breaks its own row
threads.body:
Art's sticker book has a row of six tabs (E-0023, E-0030). Five are starter sprites — Bulbasaur, Chikorita, Treecko, Turtwig, Snivy. They teach a rule in one glance: each picture is a doorway to a group of creatures. The sixth is an open book, and it breaks the rule it just taught. It is not a creature. In a row of five creatures it reads as a sixth region whose starter is a book.

Worse, that same open book is the STICKERS button he pressed to get here (visible in /home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/junior-real-375x667-hoarder/artdex-04-dex-settled.png). So the picture that means 'go to the book' is now sitting inside the book, and pressing it doesn't go anywhere — on a full save (E-0030) the grid it produces looks much like the one already on screen. That is a dead tap, and dead taps are how a four-year-old decides a control is broken.

The good news is the fix is small and stays wordless: make the ALL tab a picture that means everything at once — the five starters shrunk and overlapped, or a rainbow of the five tab colours. Anything that keeps the row's grammar of 'this picture is a group of Pokemon'.

threads.title: The little Poke Ball that says MINE, in two shapes at once
threads.body:
Put these two side by side. Fresh save, Arbok: 'NO. 0024', nothing before it (E-0026). Full save, same Arbok, same number: a small Poke Ball sits in front of it (E-0033). No word changed. Art learns 'ball beside the number = I have this one' in about two encounters, and it never lies to him.

Then the same fact gets told a second time, louder, at the bottom of the screen. Uncaught, the big button is a red ball on red and it says CATCH. Caught, that whole bar turns green and the ball is replaced by a fat check mark (compare /home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/junior-real-375x667-fresh/artdex-04-dex-settled.png with the one I generated at /home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/junior-real-375x667-hoarder/artdex-04-dex-settled.png). Colour changes, shape changes, and the meaning changes with them — that is the redundancy rule done properly. A pre-reader who confuses red and green still has ball-versus-tick; one who misses the tick still has the colour.

It even survives the broken state. In E-0033 the dex has gone blank below the header, yet the little ball is still there doing its job.

Worth a regression test: for a caught species the ball glyph renders and the action bar is green with a tick; for an uncaught one, neither. If a refactor ever ships an OWNED state that only differs by its text, this is the thing that quietly broke.

threads.title: Make each button a picture of what it is about to do
threads.body:
Look at Art's tool row (/home/kevin/pokedex/test/playtest/junior-real-375x667-hoarder/artdex-04-dex-settled.png). Six buttons. Two are arrows, and they need nothing — an arrow is a direction, he already owns it. The other three are a speaker, sparkles and a dice, each with a word underneath: CRY, SHINY, RNDM. Those three glyphs are abstractions that only resolve once you read the word, and Art cannot. A dice means 'random' to someone who has played board games with a grown-up who explained probability. To him it is a dice.

The wish: in Junior Mode, let each of those buttons be a small picture of its own result, so pressing it confirms what he already guessed.

- SHINY: draw the button as the same Pokemon he is looking at, in its shiny colours, shrunk down. The button is the answer.
- CRY: the Pokemon's own head with sound rings coming off it — his Pokemon, making a noise — instead of a generic speaker that also lives in the header.
- RNDM: a Poke Ball with a question mark, or a blurred silhouette of an unknown Pokemon, which is exactly what he gets.

Same six buttons, same layout, same code path — just glyphs that are specific to this Pokemon on this screen rather than category icons borrowed from grown-up software. And it costs nothing for Gabe, who keeps his labels.

threads.title: Super effective and useless wear the same orange badge
threads.body:
Hiker Carl's Geodude, E-0151. Three of my four moves carry an orange corner badge meaning "this will barely scratch it" and the fourth carries an orange corner badge meaning "this is the one". I zoomed both in (badges_gym_row1.png, badges_gym_bulldoze.png): same orange rounded square, same size, same corner, same two white triangles. One pair points down, one points up. That is the entire difference.

On the phone that badge is about 20px and the triangles inside it about 6px. The one tactical decision the fight asks a child to make is encoded in the direction of a 6-pixel triangle, in identical orange for yes and for no. A kid scanning the grid sees four orange dots.

It loses information at the top end too. Against Paras, Bug/Grass, Blaze Kick is a 4x hit (E-0107) and gets exactly the badge that Kakuna's plain 2x got (E-0156).

Colour is free here and this game uses colour brilliantly everywhere else. Green badge up, red badge down, and the arrow direction stops carrying the whole load.

threads.title: The enemy hits me and my HP bar doesn't move
threads.body:
Confirming F-041 from the other side of the game: normal mode, two different saves, no Junior involved.

Mid save, E-0157. I tap Blaze Kick. Kakuna's bar drops to a third, a faint "-34" drifts over the sky, and the sentence on screen reads KAKUNA USED BUG BITE! Charizard: 86/86, bar full green.

Champion save, E-0108. Same tap, same beat. PARAS USED SECRET POWER! Charizard: 168/168, full green.

So at the exact instant the game announces something hit my Pokemon, my Pokemon is visibly untouched, and the only number anywhere on screen is the damage I did to them a beat earlier, rendered in pale blue-grey on a pale blue sky (dmgnum.png). The damage does land eventually: by E-0091 Charizard is down to 75/168. It just never lands in the same frame as the sentence explaining it.

For a fight to read as a system, one link has to be airtight: their move, then my bar moves, while the words are still up. Hold the enemy's line until their damage has actually animated onto my bar, and put the number on the bar it drained.

threads.title: The spoils list isn't missing, it's above the sentence
threads.body:
Adding a detail to F-026 that should save whoever fixes it an hour of hunting through battle.js. The list is not missing. It is printed above the sentence that promises it.

E-0104, the last fight of a champion Saturday. Reading the modal top to bottom: a trophy, then a framed card holding a Geodude sprite and "Lv 8", then "TAP TO SEE IT!", then the gold XP bar, then the red headline HIKER CARL DEFEATED!, and only then "You caught their whole team:" with empty space under it.

Everything the sentence promises is already on screen, sitting about a hundred pixels higher, before the headline that would have given it meaning. So it reads as a broken reward when it is really a stacking order. Move the card below its own caption, or move the caption up to sit on top of the card.

One more thing while that modal is open: "their whole team" over a single Geodude, because Carl only owns one, reads like the other five failed to load. For a one-Pokemon trainer the line wants to be about that Pokemon.

threads.title: The move buttons run a real, correct type chart
threads.body:
I checked the maths behind every effectiveness badge in my slice and it is right, every single time.

Geodude, Rock/Ground (E-0151): Blaze Kick down, Strength down, Air Cutter down, Bulldoze up. Fire, Normal and Flying are all halved by Rock; Ground is doubled. Four for four.

Kakuna, Bug/Poison (E-0156): Blaze Kick up, Air Cutter up, Strength and Bulldoze unmarked. Fire and Flying double against Bug; Normal is flat; Ground's double on Poison cancels its half on Bug to land on exactly neutral, and the game correctly says nothing rather than guessing.

Paras, Bug/Grass (E-0107): both super-effective moves marked, both quiet ones quiet.

And it is shown before you commit, on the button, not in the log afterwards. That is the whole difference between a fight and a slot machine. Gabe can learn "fire beats bugs, not rocks" off this screen with nobody reading him a chart, and he learns it at the moment of choosing, which is the moment it sticks.

Whatever else moves inside battle.js, keep the badge computed before the turn and drawn on the button.

threads.title: Show my six on the fight screen
threads.body:
The battle screen tells me everything about the opponent and nothing about my bench. Geodude's box reads LV 8 - 1/1 (E-0151), so I know precisely how many Carl has left. My side is one Charizard and a mystery.

In a gym fight the way to my bench is a full-width SWITCH button. In a wild fight (E-0107) it appears to shrink to an unlabelled cream square in the bottom right with a small Pikachu in it (switch_wild.png). No word, no colour, nothing saying "your other five live here". When Charizard is sitting at 75/168 (E-0091), that square is the most important control on screen and the least visible one.

You already draw exactly the thing I want, one screen earlier: the gym roster (E-0150) shows every trainer's team as a neat row of little sprites.

Put that row on the battle screen for me. Six slots, my Pokemon's real sprites, greyed when fainted, tap one to switch. Gabe gets his party at a glance, Art gets six pictures instead of a word he can't read, and switching stops being a hidden move.

threads.title: Round 2 shows Round 1's ticks, so the last badge is untrackable
threads.body:
Gabe is Champion. He taps GYMS, taps ROUND 2, and the screen tells him he is finished: TRAINERS DEFEATED 58/58, and all twelve gym tiles wearing a green check (E-0067, E-0096). He opens Boulder Gym under that same Round 2 tab and gets 5/5 DEFEATED with a green check beside every trainer (E-0068).

He has not beaten a single one. I scrolled his trainer card to the bottom and the MASTER badge reads "Beat all 58 in ROUND 2 — 0/58", greyed out (my shot, spotcheck-01). Round 2 is displaying Round 1's completion data.

That is the whole endgame. The last badge in the game costs 58 fights, and the only screen that counts them is buried under a scrolling trainer card behind a CLOSE button that already clips its own bottom row. The screen Gabe actually stands on says DONE.

He will either think he already earned it and feel cheated when the badge stays grey, or he will grind 58 fights with no counter moving in front of him. Give Round 2 its own 0/58 and its own empty checkboxes.

threads.title: Round 2 pays half XP for a Lv 8 Geodude with 1 HP
threads.body:
I watched Gabe's Round 2 rematch. His Charizard is Lv 62 with 168 HP. Across the field: Hiker Carl's Geodude, LV 8, 1/1 HP (E-0069). One hit point.

The rest of the stop is the same — Lv 8, Lv 9, Lv 10, Lv 11, Lv 13 — and every rematch button is stamped REMATCH — HALF XP (E-0068). So the game's post-Champion content is its weakest opponents, explicitly advertised at half rate, and the last badge asks for 58 of them.

As an economy that is upside down. Every hour Gabe put in to reach Lv 62 made the only content he has left pay less, and the button says so out loud. "HALF XP" is the first thing he reads on the screen that is supposed to be his reward for winning the game.

The fix is not more XP on the same fight — it is a fight worth having. Scale Round 2 trainers to the player's top level (Lv 62 Geodude, full team, full HP) and pay full. Same 58 names, a real ladder.

threads.title: Three free balls that all say the same thing, one that's never spent
threads.body:
The ball drawer is the same in both endgame saves (E-0109, E-0147). POKÉBALL, GREAT BALL, ULTRA BALL — no quantity on any of them, so all three are infinite — and all three carry the identical line BETTER WHEN WEAKENED. Underneath, MASTER BALL, the only one with a number, and the only one with a different promise: NEVER FAILS.

So there is no decision on this screen. Three buttons that are free and, as far as the words go, the same; one that is scarce and strictly better. A kid taps the top one forever.

And the scarce one never gets spent. Gabe the hoarder has CAUGHT 620 and still holds MASTER BALLS x9. Champion Gabe has CAUGHT 202 and x5 (E-0145, spotcheck-01). Across 620 catches nothing in the game was ever hard enough to be worth the good ball, so the stock only ever goes up.

Either give the three free balls real, visible odds (a 1-2-3 pip strip like the moves already use), or give the Master Ball something worth spending it on — a legendary that a normal ball genuinely won't hold.

threads.title: Every locked badge names its price and my exact distance
threads.body:
This is the best-designed thing in the game's economy and I want it nailed down before something breaks it.

On the trainer card, every badge Gabe has not earned yet still tells him two numbers: what it costs, and how close he is. CURATOR — Catch 300 Pokémon — 202/300. PROFESSOR — Catch all 649! — 202/649. EXPERT — Raise one to Lv 60 — 55/60. MASTER — Beat all 58 in ROUND 2 — 0/58 (E-0072, E-0145).

That is a proper goal ladder. A seven-year-old can look at 55/60 and know exactly what tonight is for. He can look at 202/300 and know it is a project, not an evening. Nothing is a mystery box, nothing is "???", and the greyed-out ones are still legible enough to plan against — which is the whole reason a long game keeps a kid.

Please keep it: every locked badge renders its requirement text AND a live progress fraction. If a future badge ever ships without both halves, that is a regression. It is also, notably, the only place in the app that tells the truth about Round 2.

threads.title: Tell me what today's quest actually pays
threads.body:
TODAY'S QUESTS gives Gabe a checklist: "Win a battle 0/1", "Catch a ROCK type 0/1", "Catch a WATER type 0/1", "Evolve 2 Pokémon 0/2" (spotcheck-01). The hoarder save gets "Go exploring 3 times 0/3", "Catch one in the OCEAN 0/1", "Evolve a Pokémon 0/1" (E-0145).

Seven quests across two saves, and not one of them says what it is worth. The badges two inches above them are exemplary about this — cost and progress, every time. The quests are asking for work and naming no wage.

I would put the prize right on the row, as a picture: a ball sprite, a sparkle, a small number. "Catch a ROCK type → 🔴 x3". Then EXPLORE has a reason to exist (both endgame saves show EXPLORES 0), the free-ball problem above gets a currency, and Gabe can choose which quest to do first — which is the only thing that makes a quest list a game instead of a chore list.

One caution, since these reset daily: show the prize, but never show a streak he can break.
rule_risk: Rule 3 (never take something away): daily quests reset, so any reward attached to them must not create a streak or a loss the boys can feel.

threads.title: Deep Forest promises BUG GRASS BIRD, hands over Poison
threads.body:
The DEEP FOREST card (E-0106, E-0089) makes exactly one promise under its tree: BUG · GRASS · BIRD. I entered it three times across two saves and it kept that promise once. E-0107 gave me PARAS (Bug/Grass — perfect, and PokeAPI puts it in 'forest' too). E-0130 gave me EKANS, a pure Poison snake PokeAPI files under 'grassland' — and the game HAS a TALL GRASS habitat. E-0090 gave me KOFFING, pure Poison, PokeAPI habitat 'urban'. Neither belongs under that tree by the card's own type list or by PokeAPI's habitat.

It reads like species with no home in these nine habitats get dumped into the forest. Gabe picks DEEP FOREST because he wants a Butterfree, and gets a poison snake; the one label on the card stops meaning anything.

Two smaller things on the same line: BIRD is not a Pokémon type — the word is FLYING, and Gabe will meet FLYING on every card and every other game. And DRAGON'S DEN reads DRAGON · ULTRA RARE, which puts a rarity where a type goes.

threads.title: Level 57 Koffing: the number grows, the species never does
threads.body:
Every wild Pokémon I met on a champion-grade save was a baby species wearing a big number. EKANS at LV 50 (E-0130). KOFFING at LV 57 (E-0090). PARAS at LV 57 (E-0107). In the real games Ekans becomes Arbok at 22, Paras becomes Parasect at 24, Koffing becomes Weezing at 35 — I checked all three against PokeAPI. A level 57 Koffing is a thing that cannot exist in the wild anywhere else in Pokémon.

The level scaling itself is lovely: the wild is tuned to Gabe's Lv 62 Charizard (E-0107), so nothing is a pushover and nothing is a wall. It's only the species pool that never grew up with him. So the reward for becoming Champion is that the same Caterpie-tier creatures show up with bigger HP bars, and Gabe's dex will never once show him an evolved form appearing in the grass.

The fix is the one the real games use: as a habitat's level band climbs, swap the base forms out for their evolutions. Same code path, and DEEP FOREST at Lv 57 starts handing over Parasect and Butterfree.

threads.title: Shiny sparkle, ordinary sprite: my black Charizard is orange
threads.body:
The hoarder box (E-0110) puts a ✨ on exactly twelve cards — #001 Bulbasaur through #012 Butterfree — and the champion box, which owns no shinies, has none (E-0070). So the sparkle means shiny. But all twelve sprites are the ordinary palette. Shiny Charizard is famously black; the card at #006 shows the same orange Charizard the champion has.

The A/B is clean and it's the same page twice: E-0111 is the hoarder's Charmander dex entry (shiny-flagged) and E-0071 is the champion's (not), and the two sprites are pixel-for-pixel the same orange lizard. PokeAPI hands over front_shiny for every one of these, and the game already knows how to draw it — there's a SHINY button sitting right there on the same screen.

A shiny is the single rarest thing a seven-year-old can own, and the whole point is that it LOOKS different. Right now the only proof Gabe has is a small star, and every sparkle in his box is a promise the picture doesn't keep.

threads.title: The species data is real, and it is right
threads.body:
I came in expecting invented stats and I could not find one. Charmander's page (E-0111, E-0071) reads NO. 0004, FIRE, HT 0.6 m, WT 8.5 kg, GENUS 'Lizard Pokémon' — every field matches PokeAPI exactly, right down to the genus string most fan projects paraphrase. Pikachu is NO. 0025, ELECTRIC, and its habitat chip is the forest tree, not the power plant its type would suggest — because PokeAPI genuinely files Pikachu under 'forest'. Somebody wired that to the real data instead of guessing from the type.

Charizard's four moves in battle (E-0107) are BLAZE KICK, AIR CUTTER, STRENGTH, SECRET POWER/MEGA KICK. I checked all five against Charizard's learnset: every one is legal, and the tile colours are the real type colours — Fire orange, Flying blue, Normal grey. And the PC box runs #001 Bulbasaur, #002 Ivysaur, #003 Venusaur, #004 Charmander in true family order (E-0070).

This is the layer that makes Gabe trust the game when he compares it to his cards. Please keep the dex header and the movepool sourced from PokeAPI — never hand-write these.

threads.title: Show me the family: Charmander to Charmeleon to Charizard
threads.body:
Charmander's page (E-0111) has CRY, SHINY, RNDM, DATA — and nowhere on it does the game mention that #005 and #006 are the same creature growing up. The box already knows (E-0070 sits Charmander, Charmeleon and Charizard side by side in order), and PokeAPI hands over the whole chain for free.

What I want is a strip of three sprites under the big one: small, medium, huge, with a little arrow between them and the level it happens at. Tap one, jump to it.

This is the one bit of Pokémon knowledge that is entirely pictures. Art cannot read CHARMELEON, but he can absolutely see that the small orange one turns into the big red one turns into the enormous winged one, and that is the whole idea of evolution delivered without a single word. For Gabe it's the thing he'd otherwise go and look up on a phone. Grey out the ones he hasn't caught and it doubles as a to-do list — three empty silhouettes he wants to fill in.

threads.title: Champion's circuit says 58/58 and offers nothing
threads.body:
I opened the Gym Circuit on the champion save (E-0067, and again at E-0096 after a whole session of fighting). There is exactly one number on it: TRAINERS DEFEATED 58/58, in grey. The headline card is CROWN ELITE FOUR + CHAMPION with all five progress boxes filled solid green — and the crossed swords "go fight this" icon still sitting on the right of a fight he finished weeks ago. Under it, twelve badges, all ticked. Under that, a heal button and a versus button. That's the whole endgame screen.

Per your own changelog, ROUND 2 is the entire point of this save state: 58 trainers back at +15 levels, Hiker Carl at Lv23, a MASTER BADGE at the end. On screen it is a chip at the top that is filled gold while ROUND 1 sits on plain cream paper — so the tab that looks pressed is the one you are not on, nothing beneath it has changed, and the counter reads 58/58 instead of 0/58. Walking into Boulder from here still gives Lv 8 Carl (E-0068).

Make ROUND 2 the hero card, with its own counter and its own empty boxes.

threads.title: Endurance HP is invisible; healing is one grey line
threads.body:
HP carrying from trainer to trainer inside a stop is a great idea. The problem is you can't see it anywhere.

On the Boulder Gym page (E-0068, E-0105) there is no HP at all: a header reading "5/5 DEFEATED — WIN TO CATCH THEIR TEAM!", then five trainer cards. No team strip, no bars, and no Poke Center button — the heal lives one screen back on the circuit (E-0096), so to check on his team mid-stop Gabe has to leave the stop.

Then the payoff. I pressed the big pink POKE CENTER — HEAL TEAM, and the entire response was one line of small pink text at the very bottom of the page, below the versus button: "YOUR TEAM IS FULLY HEALED!" That line is literally the only pixel difference between E-0096 and E-0097. Nothing moved, nothing flashed, no team shown, no bars refilling.

So he can't tell whether he needed healing, and after a rough fight he can't tell whether he's about to walk into Leader Rocko at 12 HP. Put a six-slot HP strip at the top of the stop page with the heal button beside it, and let the bars visibly refill.

threads.title: Every rematch is a Lv8 fight labelled HALF XP
threads.body:
On the champion save, Boulder Gym is five identical green cards, each carrying 🔁 REMATCH — HALF XP (E-0068, E-0105). "HALF XP" is the single most repeated string on the page — five times down one screen. The trainers behind those buttons are Lv 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13. The Charizard that walks in is Lv 62 (E-0069): a level sixty-two dragon against a one-Pokemon level eight Geodude, for half of almost nothing.

Two separate problems. First, the button leads with the deduction instead of the prize — the actual reason to rematch ("WIN TO CATCH THEIR TEAM") is printed once, in small type, in the header. A seven-year-old reads five green buttons that all say his reward is halved. Second, there is no route from this screen to a version of these same five trainers that would still be a fight.

Label the button with what he wins — 🔁 REMATCH → CATCH THEIR TEAM — and if a harder tier of this stop exists, put a gold "HIKER CARL Lv 23 — FULL XP" card right beside the Lv 8 one. (Adjacent to F-008, which is about the ceremony after the win. This is about the offer before it.)
rule_risk: never take something away from a child: the only label on a returning player's button is a halved reward

threads.title: The stop roster shows exactly what you're walking into
threads.body:
Boulder Gym's trainer list is the best-designed screen in my slice, and it renders identically on the mid and champion saves (E-0150, E-0068).

Five cards, top to bottom. A big portrait of the lead Pokemon. Then the trainer's actual team sprites, in the number they actually field — Carl one, Sandy two, Ruin Maniac Leo two, Leader Rocko three. A name. A one-line taunt in the trainer's own voice ("My fossils are old. My skills are TIMELESS."). And a level in the corner climbing 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, with LEADER ROCKO last.

Gabe can read the whole stop before he commits a single turn: how many fights, how many Pokemon each, how steep the ladder. And it tells the truth — I tapped the first card and got exactly the Geodude Lv 8 the card had drawn (E-0069).

Please keep this contract when Round 2 lands: sprites on the card = the real team, corner level = the real level, leader last. Worth a smoke check that the first trainer card's printed level equals the level of the Pokemon that actually appears in the battle.

threads.title: A gauntlet: five trainers, one health bar
threads.body:
The circuit already owns every part a tournament needs and never holds one. HP carries between trainers inside a stop. The stops are five-trainer ladders that already escalate. Badges already hang on a wall.

So: once a stop is cleared, put a GAUNTLET card on it. All five trainers back to back. No Poke Center in between. The six you started with are the six you finish with. Clear it and a ribbon lights up next to that stop's badge.

That is real difficulty without inventing a single new trainer or raising a single level, and it makes a Lv 8–13 roster mean something again to a Lv 62 team — which is exactly the problem on the champion's Boulder page today.

It is also rules-safe: he opts in, and if he falls over at trainer four nothing is taken from him. He keeps the badge, keeps the Pokemon, and the ribbon is simply not lit yet.

Right now the champion's circuit ends at a heal button (E-0096). This gives him something to press — and gives the ROUND 2 tab a second thing to be about.

threads.title: Tapping a box Pokemon throws you out of the box
threads.body:
Gabe has 620 caught. I opened his PC (E-0110), scrolled, and tapped Charmander at #004. The PC did not open a detail card — it slammed shut and dumped me on the main dex screen (E-0111). Same thing again mid-session: tapped one box Pokemon, ejected to dex; tapped another, ejected again (E-0139, E-0140).

Two things go wrong at 620. First, my place is gone. Reopening PC puts me back at the top of G1, so any tap costs me the whole scroll again — and in a 620 box that scroll was the expensive part. Second, it shows me the wrong Pokemon. The one I tapped is Gabe's SHINY Charmander at Lv 55; the dex page shows the ordinary species entry, SHINY button unpressed, no level, no nickname (E-0111). I asked about MY Charmander and got the encyclopedia article.

Art's box does the right thing here — his tap opens a little card in place, box still behind it (E-0031). Gabe's box should do that too: open, close, and I am still exactly where I was.

threads.title: The ALL tab hangs half off the right edge
threads.body:
The generation tabs across Gabe's box are the only way to cut 620 Pokemon down to something walkable, and on a 390-wide phone the strip does not fit. Open the PC cold and the leftmost tab is already sliced — you can read "1 5 1" but the label above it is chopped by the screen edge — while on the right, the ALL tab is reduced to a lone "A" and "6 2 0" falling off the edge (E-0110, and identical in E-0146).

There is no arrow, no fade, no half-peeking next tab that says "keep swiping." It just ends. The tab I most want as a hoarder — the one holding all 620 — is the one that is barely there, and the tab I am currently standing on is clipped too, so I cannot tell it is selected without squinting at the brighter green fill.

This is a small fix with a big payoff: shrink the tabs so all six fit, or put a visible chevron at each end. Right now the strip looks finished when it isn't.

threads.title: Art sees nine Pokemon at a time out of 620
threads.body:
I opened Art's box on the small phone with 620 caught (E-0030). Measuring the screenshot: the favourites shelf, the team strip and the tab row eat the top 242 of 667 pixels before a single box Pokemon appears, and the fat green BACK bar takes the bottom 90. What is left shows three full rows of three, plus a sliver — call it nine or ten Pokemon on screen at once.

Nine out of 620. That is roughly 65 screenfuls of flicking. Gabe at least has a search box; Art cannot type, so scroll is his only tool, and the gen tabs are his only filter. If he wants the Snorlax he caught on Tuesday and it isn't in his team strip, he is not going to find it. He will give up, and a 4-year-old giving up on his own collection is the outcome this whole screen exists to prevent.

The cards are lovely and the right size — I would not shrink them. I would give him a shorter header and something better than scrolling (see my wish). Confirmed unchanged after heavy mashing (E-0036).

threads.title: Both brothers get the same six-slot team, lead marked without words
threads.body:
This is the one part of the collection UI that scales cleanly and I want it nailed down before someone refactors it.

Gabe's box (E-0110) and Art's box (E-0030) show the exact same object: six slots, same order, same sprites, lead in position one. Gabe's lead has a gold border and a star; Art's lead has a gold-tinted cell and a small gold mark. Neither needs the word LEAD to know which one goes first — it is colour and position, which is precisely the rule CLAUDE.md sets out. Art can point at his Charizard and know it's the one that comes out first, and it is the same picture his big brother sees.

It also holds up on the small phone. All six of Art's slots fit on one row at 375 with nothing clipped (E-0030, E-0036) — worth pinning as a regression test, because other reviewers found the normal-mode strip losing a slot at that width.

One caveat while you're in there: Art's gold tint is tan-on-cream and much quieter than Gabe's gold border. Push it a shade.

threads.title: Let me shelve by newest and by sparkle, not just by region
threads.body:
Gabe's trainer card says CAUGHT 620 and SHINIES 12 (E-0145). Twelve. Those twelve are the twelve he is proudest of, and there is no way on earth to reach them except scrolling 620 cards looking for a gold sparkle. In this save they happen to sit at #001-#012 so the box looks sparkly at the top (E-0110); after the next shiny at #430 that stops being true.

Same problem with the newest catch. Catch something and it files itself into dex order, so the thing you just did lands at row 143 and vanishes. The moment of pride has nowhere to go.

I would add a small row of picture chips beside the gen tabs: a Poke Ball for NEWEST, a sparkle for SHINY, a star for FAVES. Icons only, so they work identically in Art's box — he cannot read G1 either, and a sparkle chip that fills his screen with just the special ones is the single best thing you could hand a 4-year-old with 620 Pokemon. Nothing is removed; it is a lens, not a filter that hides.

threads.title: The versus button calls the other brother "P 2"
threads.body:
On Gabe's GYM CIRCUIT the shared-play bar reads "VS  GABE  VS  P 2". On Art's it reads "VS  ART  VS  P 2". Same button, same anonymous second seat, whichever brother is holding the phone.

The game knows both boys' names everywhere else — the chip in the top-left says GABE or ART, the box header says GABE'S PC BOX and ART'S PC BOX. The one screen that exists because there are two children is the screen that drops a name. And the second half is styled fainter than the first: GABE is white on red, P 2 is grey-blue on blue. The younger seat is literally lower contrast.

Both halves are words, so Art has nothing at all here. He cannot read ART, he cannot read P 2, and the red-and-blue bar gives him no clue which end is him.

In these runs player 2 was never named — which is the state every family is in on day one, before anyone thinks to open Settings. That is exactly the moment the second child matters. Put each boy's lead Pokémon sprite on his half of the bar and the button works before anyone types anything.

threads.title: Art's quest reward is Gabe's quest reward, word for word
threads.body:
I put the Junior shot and the normal shot next to each other and they are the same panel, pixel for pixel: a star, "QUEST COMPLETE!", "Catch a GRASS type — done!", "+30 XP to your lead Pokémon!", and a button that says AWESOME!. Sentence case, lowercase words, an accented é, four lines of prose.

Junior Mode rewrites the dex, the battle move buttons and the PC box for Art. It does not touch the one panel that hands out rewards.

What that costs is bigger than one modal. Gabe can read "catch a Grass type", decide to go and do it, and come back for the star. Art can only be surprised by stars. The entire quest system is a game his brother plays deliberately and he receives by accident. Nothing is taken from him — he gets the XP either way — but he never gets to aim, and aiming is the fun part.

Say it as pictures: the Grass type tile he needs, then the same tile with a tick. He already reads type colour fine elsewhere.

(Both shots are filenamed STILL-OPEN — a second modal was queued behind the first.)
